Type-II superionic conductors, which undergo continuous temperature-driven transitions between low and high ionic conductivity regimes are strong candidates for high-performance solid state electrolytes, but the transition mechanism is not sufficiently understood. In this study, we investigate the archetypical superionic conductors Li2O and Li2S with the antifluorite structure using long-time-scale molecular dynamics simulations with an Allegro machine-learning force field (MLFF) trained on density functional theory data selected using an on-the-fly active learning procedure. To this end, superionic transitions are identified around 1450 K for Li2O and around 1100 K for Li2S through continuous peaks in the heat capacity. Diffusion coefficients and concentration of Frenkel defects are found to exhibit strong non-Arrhenius behavior coinciding with the superionic transition where both diffusion activation energy and defect formation energy decrease significantly across the transition. This suggests a self-enhanced spontaneous defect formation mechanism, which drives the superionic transition and promotes increased ionic diffusion. These results identifies the microscopic origin of type-II superionic behavior as a result of correlated defect formation and support the design of improved solid-state electrolytes.

item.title: Cost-effective nanorough black nickel-based SERS substrates with statistically validated spatial uniformity
item.description: Reliable surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrates must combine high enhancement with spatially uniform and reproducible responses. Here, hierarchical rough black nickel (b-Ni) substrates were fabricated by electrodeposition and acid etching and coated with Ag or Au layers (5–50 nm). Their SERS performance was systematically evaluated using 4-mercaptobenzoic acid (4-MBA) and large-area Raman mapping (1.5 × 1.5 mm2; 900 spectra per substrate), supported by statistical analysis of signal intensity, spatial variability, response distribution, and inter-band correlation. Metrics included median signed band areas, relative standard deviation (RSD), the median absolute deviation (MAD)-based coefficient of variation, the contribution of the 10% highest-response positions to the total positive response, and Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient. Ag-coated b-Ni substrates exhibited substantially stronger and more spatially uniform enhancement than Au-coated substrates, with performance increasing with Ag thickness. The 50 nm b-Ni/Ag architecture provided the optimal combination of signal strength and spatial reproducibility. Control experiments with bare b-Ni and flat Ag and Au films deposited on polished silicon confirmed that the enhancement arises from the synergistic effect of hierarchical b-Ni micro/nanoroughness and the plasmonic noble-metal coating. These results establish Ag-coated b-Ni as a simple, low-cost, and scalable platform for robust SERS measurements, reducing the need for extensive spatial screening.

item.title: Binding Mode of the Heterocyclic Amine 2-Amino-9H-pyrido[2,3-b] indole (AαC) to DNA Elucidated by Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Simulation
item.description: Background: 2-Amino-9H-pyrido[2,3-b]indole (AαC) is a mutagenic and carcinogenic heterocyclic aromatic amine formed by pyrolysis of proteins in cooked meat and present in tobacco smoke. After metabolic activation to a reactive nitrenium ion, it modifies DNA covalently, mainly at guanine. How AαC first associates with DNA, before any covalent bond forms, is not well understood. Methods: We docked AαC to three B-DNA dodecamers (PDB IDs 1BNA, 2Z2G and 2HKC) with PatchDock and FireDock, and ran explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the docked complexes in NAMD 2.13 with the CHARMM36 force field (1BNA: 10 ns; 2Z2G: 50 ns; NPT, 300 K, 0.15 M NaCl). Results: AαC bound in the minor groove of all three dodecamers, with global binding energies of -50.08 (1BNA), -53.41 (2Z2G) and -45.22 kcal/mol (2HKC). Atomic van der Waals terms contributed -16.41 to -18.36 kcal/mol, and single hydrogen bonds to thymine, guanine or adenine oxygen atoms were identified (2.2–2.8 Å). In the simulations AαC remained bound with a low, stable backbone RMSD, whereas the DNA backbone fluctuated considerably more. The minor-groove poses were poorly oriented for covalent attack when the base pairs were intact and canonical. Conclusions: Neutral AαC forms stable, groove-bound non-covalent complexes with B-DNA, but these complexes do not by themselves position the amine for C8-guanine adduct formation. Local distortion of the DNA, or the charged nitrenium ion, may be required. The complexes presented here serve as starting structures for ongoing quantum-mechanical studies of nitrenium ion stability and covalent adduct formation.

item.title: The Disproportionation of Hydrogen Peroxide by Prototype Keggin Polyoxometalates
item.description: Polyoxometalates (POMs) have been widely investigated as enzyme-mimetic compounds because of their ability to activate hydrogen peroxide for its disproportionation into water and oxygen (catalase reactivity), or use it as terminal oxidant for organic transformations (peroxidase reactivity). Here, we report how the prototype Keggin-type POMs H3[PW12O40] ({PW12}) and H3[PMo12O40] ({PMo12}) interact with hydrogen peroxide and lead to H2O2 activation and conversion to water and oxygen. Experimental and computational approaches were combined to elucidate the reaction pathways and intermediates formed, showing that formation of hydroperoxyl radical species is the dominant path, while hydroxyl radicals, if formed, are consumed before they diffuse into the bulk solution. This understanding provides insight into one of the most widely used POM-based oxidation processes and enables knowledge-based control of reactivity.

item.title: Enhanced Paper-Based DNA Adsorption and Point-of-Care Detection of High-Risk Human Papillomaviruses 16 and 18.
item.description: Cervical cancer screening in low-resource settings requires molecular diagnostics that integrate rapid DNA extraction with sensitive, low-cost DNA amplification and detection. Here, we present a paper-based DNA detection (PDD) platform that introduces two mechanistic advances for decentralized HPV diagnostics. First, we establish a centrifuge-free DNA isolation strategy based on ethanol-assisted capture of DNA onto cellulose paper to provide high-yield DNA. Second, we introduce a coffee-ring-based fluorescence-sensing mechanism that converts the spatial redistribution of PicoGreen-labeled amplified products into a quantitative readout. We report, for the first time, that acid-pretreated cellulose (APC) paper captures DNA efficiently relative to untreated paper, identifying substrate pH as a critical factor in paper-based DNA extraction. FTIR analysis and zeta potential measurements revealed that APC paper retained DNA efficiently primarily through hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions, respectively. Moreover, the mechanism behind the coffee ring-based amplified DNA detection was attributed to the chromatographic and evaporation effects. DNA is quantified using peripheral fluorescence intensity (PFI), enabling robust discrimination between positive and negative reactions. The integrated platform detected HPV16 and HPV18 with a limit of detection of 10 copies μL⁻¹. Clinical evaluation of 52 cervical samples demonstrated 100% specificity for both HPV16 and HPV18, 100% sensitivity for HPV18, and 85.7% sensitivity for HPV16 compared with an IVD-approved real-time PCR assay. By combining mechanistically guided DNA isolation with physics-based spatial DNA detection, this work advances paper-based molecular diagnostics beyond conventional intensity-based assays and provides a simple, inexpensive, and field-deployable strategy for point-of-care detection of HR HPVs.

item.title: A sustainability-aware self-driving laboratory
item.description: Self-driving laboratories are transforming experimental science, shifting laboratory operation from human-centric schedules towards continuous robotic execution. Beyond accelerating discovery, this transition creates new flexibility in when scientific research consumes electricity, offering an opportunity to coordinate experimental activity with changing electricity-system conditions. Here, we develop and deploy a dynamic, sustainability-aware laboratory-level scheduling framework that combines reinforcement learning with constraint programming to jointly optimize completion time and electricity cost under scientific constraints. Physical execution of 36 experimental tasks spanning six chemical workflow categories shortened completion time by 39.1% and reduced estimated electricity costs by 28.9% relative to a simulated human-centric scheduling baseline. Across five representative tariff cases, estimated per-workflow savings were equivalent to the cost of 0.83–9.14 kWh of off-peak electricity. Our findings demonstrate how self-driving laboratories can translate operational freedom into electricity-demand flexibility, establishing energy responsiveness as a design consideration for scientific research infrastructure.

item.title: Raman Spectroscopy–Evolved Gas Analysis–Mass Spectrometry Provides Insight into Thermoset Thermal Degradation
item.description: Raman spectroscopy–evolved gas analysis–mass spectrometry (RS-EGA-MS) was developed to investigate the thermal degradation of a bisphenol A–based thermoset. A new interface was developed that couples a Stokes/anti-Stokes Raman probe to a Frontier microfurnace used for EGA-MS. This new advancement enables collection of Raman spectra from a sample undergoing thermal degradation while simultaneously monitoring evolved gases from degradation. Changes in the Raman spectra were evident at the early stages of thermal degradation and corresponded to loss of bisphenol A monomer units. Later stages of thermal degradation resulted in intense fluorescence that overwhelmed the detector; anti-Stokes RS was used to interrogate these higher-temperature regions. Multiple char-forming regions which corresponded to the formation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) were identified at these higher temperatures. The formation of naphthalene and fluoranthene were identified as important PAH products in the overall char formation of the bisphenol A based thermoset. This work demonstrates the successful development of RS-EGA-MS and provides new insight into high-temperature

item.title: Copper-Catalyzed Borylation of 2-Bromostyrenes via 1,3-Bromine and 1,4-Boryl Group Migrations
item.description: Arylboronates are valuable synthetic intermediates for constructing C–C and C–X bonds. While the coppercatalyzed borylation of aryl halides has been reported, synthesizing 2-borylstyrenes from the corresponding aryl halides remains a challenge because the alkene is incompatible with conventional borylation methods. Herein, we turn this side reaction into the trigger of a productive cascade, enabling the copper-catalyzed borylation of 2-bromostyrenes with diboron reagents. The sequence comprises borylcupration, 1,3-bromine migration to form an arylcopper, intramolecular attack of the arylcopper on boron to give a cyclic borate, and copper-assisted debromination that restores the alkenyl group. Overall, the boryl group undergoes a 1,4-migration from C(sp3) to C(sp2), with the alkene serving as a transient relay. The detailed reaction mechanism for 1,4-boryl group migration was revealed by using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The reaction tolerates chloro substituent and borylates dibromostyrenes site-selectively and is readily scalable to the gram scale.

item.title: Factorised Cartesian Atomic Cluster Expansion for Low-Cost Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
item.description: Machine-learning interatomic potentials can reach the accuracy of density functional theory at a fraction of its cost, but the most accurate equivariant models remain expensive, mainly because of the tensor operations they perform for every pair of neighbouring atoms. We present FACE, a factorised Cartesian atomic cluster expansion that removes this bottleneck. Each neighbour contributes only a small set of radial functions and messages, and all mixing of feature channels is done once per atom, so the cost per neighbour no longer grows with the size of the model. Custom GPU kernels evaluate the remaining steps, and long-range electrostatics, dispersion and short-range repulsion attach through a single interface. We show that the training divergences we encountered originate in how the network weights are scaled, and we introduce a distillation scheme in which an ensemble generates additional, uncertainty-checked training data. On five rMD17 molecules, with identical training budgets and hardware, FACE is about as accurate as a 64-channel MACE model (over three seeds: better on one molecule, within the seed spread on two, 7–14% higher force errors on two), while it is 5.7 times faster at inference (4.9 times at the same cutoff) and needs 3.5–3.9 times less GPU memory. Training costs about the same per step. Distillation lowers the energy and force errors of a single aspirin model by 20% at fixed width, to 2.26 meV and 6.74 meV/Å, close to the published MACE values (2.2 and 6.6), and the distilled model runs stably in molecular dynamics.

item.title: Reassignment of the Near-Infrared Absorption of Dioxidized Rare-Earth Porphyrin Double-Decker Complexes: Identification of a Nearly Dark Lowest Excited State
item.description: The intense near-infrared band (700–1250 nm) of dioxidized porphyrin double-decker complexes, characterized by a metal ion sandwiched between two porphyrinato ligands bearing two holes in total, has been assigned to the HOMO→LUMO transition for three decades. Herein, we demonstrate that this band does not correspond to the lowest excited state. In the spectra of [Y(oep)2]+ and [Tb(oep)2]+ (oep = octaethylporphyrinato), we observed a weak band near 1430 nm, with 2–3% of the absorbance of the intense band (at 812 nm and 830 nm) and a much smaller dependence on the metal. Time-dependent density functional theory calculations with an optimally tuned functional assigned the weak and intense bands to S1 and S3, respectively, i.e., a configuration-interaction pair of the HOMO→LUMO and HOMO−1→LUMO excitations. As observed in crystal structures reported earlier, the two rings are twisted by 30–36°, which lowers the symmetry from D4d (45°) to D4. The weak band S1 is symmetry-forbidden in D4d and owes its low intensity to this twist. The calculated slope of S3 against the ionic radius was within 3% of the experimental value, whereas S1 was nearly independent of the metal. Therefore, the lowest excited states of these strongly coupled π dimers are nearly dark.

item.title: PCl3-Mediated Surface Editing Enables Highly Emissive InP/ZnS Quantum Dots
item.description: Surface chemistry governs the optical performance of InP quantum dots (QDs), but strategies for preparing highly emissive InP/ZnS materials often rely on hazardous fluoride treatments. Here, treatment of carboxylate-capped InP QDs with PCl3 before ZnS shell growth increases the photoluminescence quantum yield from 5.5% to 70% without HF. 31P NMR spectroscopy and time-resolved small angle neutron scattering show that PCl3 removes surface carboxylates through formation of tricarboxyphosphite species. PCl3 treatment alone does not enhance emission, demonstrating that surface modification instead enables more effective passivation during shelling. These results establish controlled ligand stripping as an HF-free strategy for engineering the InP/ZnS interface and reveal how surface coordination can modulate the electronic structure and subsequent passivation of InP nanocrystals.

item.title: Hydrosilane-Dependent Regiodivergence for Rhodium-Catalyzed Dearomative Hydrosilylation of Quinolines
item.description: Regiodivergent dearomative hydroelementation (E = Si, B) of quinolines represent a powerful, atomeconomic strategy for the synthesis of biologically valuable 1,2- and 1,4-dihydroquinolines (DHQ) scaffolds. However, achieving such regiodivergent H[E] additions at the C2 and C4 positions within a unified catalytic system remains highly challenging. Herein, we report a simple [Rh(cod)Cl]2/PPh3 catalytic system that enables regioselective hydride incorporation dictated solely by the choice of hydrosilane (Ph2SiH2 vs. Me2RSiH, R = Et or Ph). While the Ph2SiH2-mediated 1,2-hydrosilylation protocol proceeds efficiently at 23 oC, the 1,4-hydrosilylation with Me2EtSiH requires a prolonged reaction time or an elevated temperature (23 to 50 oC) to achieve high yields. Preliminary mechanistic studies under the Ph2SiH2 vs. Me2PhSiH systems indicate that (i) chloro-free, phosphine-ligated Rh hydride species in situ generated during the initiation stage serves as the key resting species; (ii) a classic Chalk–Harrod sequence operates to yield the 1,2-DHQ irrespective of the hydrosilane used; (iii) the Me2PhSiH system promotes a facile isomerization of the kinetic 1,2-DHQ product to the 1,4-DHQ via an exclusive 3,4-hydrorhodation process; and (iv) the dearomative 1,2-hydrorhodation is reversible under the Ph2SiH2 system and the liberated 1,2-DHQ is completely resistant to subsequent isomerization.

item.title: Anomalous Polarization Driven Quantum Confined Stark Effect in Halide Perovskite Polymer Quantum Structures for Single Layer Electroluminescence
item.description: The quantum-confined Stark effect (QCSE) has emerged as a powerful mechanism for electrically tuning the optical properties of semiconductors. Through QCSE-induced band-structure modulation, we show that the soft-lattice ionic species and electroactive polymer interact in an anomalous polarization field mediating ion conduction, beyond the conventional bias-driven migration. The stability and magnitude of this conduction channel are governed by the spatial distribution of bound charges at the polarized interface, tunable through external poling. Single layer Li+-free light-emitting electrochemical cells (LEECs) with a PAN:PEO:MAPbBr3 composite were fabricated. The resulting anomalous internal electric field not only lowers the turn-on voltage to ~ 3 V by assisting charge injection but also imprints a measurable Quantum Confined Stark Effect (QCSE) on the embedded quantum dots. The results establish polarization-driven ion conduction as a powerful mechanism for designing next-generation solid-state optoelectronics.

item.title: Photochemical Oxidation of Dilute Methane Using a Filter-Based System for Air-Treatment Applications
item.description: Atmospheric methane (CH4) removal is challenging because of its low concentration and chemical stability under dilute conditions. Here, we demonstrate a filter-based photochemical system for dilute CH4 oxidation designed for potential integration into ventilation and air-treatment applications. A continuous-flow reactor incorporating UV-C irradiation (190–220 nm), a TiO2coated filter and an activated-carbon filter was tested at 10–50 ppm CH4, 25 °C and 1 bar under dry and humid conditions, at light intensities ranging from 4 to 59 W/m2 and flow rates of 100–300 mL/min. The downstream 4 mm activated-carbon filter reduced UV-C generated ozone (O3) to below the detection limit. CH4 conversion increased with light intensity and humidity and decreased with increasing flow rate and, under dry conditions, with increasing CH4 concentration. At 10 ppm and 100 mL/min, conversion reached 96% under humid conditions at 59 W/m2, compared with 73% under dry conditions. Significant conversion was also observed without the TiO2-coated filter, demonstrating that gas-phase photochemistry is the dominant oxidation pathway, while the TiO2-coated filter provided an additional 4–14% CH4 conversion improvement. Water vapour approximately doubled the effective removal rate. Apparent quantum yields (AQYs) for the overall photochemical system ranged from 9.3 × 10−3% at 10 ppm to 0.2% at 50 ppm, exceeding those previously obtained for TiO2-based photocatalytic oxidation under comparable dilute-CH4 conditions [1]. An advection–diffusion–reaction model reproduced the experimental trends across irradiance, humidity, concentration and flow rate. This work establishes filter-based UV-C photochemistry as a potential route for coupling dilute CH4 mitigation with existing airtreatment infrastructure.

item.title: Strain-Tunable Electron–Phonon Coupling Collapse in Oxide Perovskites: A First-Principles Route to Suppressed Hot-Carrier Thermalization
item.description: Hot-carrier thermalization constitutes the dominant energy loss channel in perovskite photovoltaics, yet the role of epitaxial strain in controlling this process remains largely unexplored from first principles. We present a systematic firstprinciples study of strain-dependent hot-carrier cooling rates in six inorganic perovskiteshalides CsSnI3, CsSnBr3, and CsCaCl3, and oxides BaSnO3, BaZrO3, and KTaO3across a ±2% biaxial strain window. Eliashberg spectral functions ω2F (ε) are computed via density functional perturbation theory and Wannier interpolation, from which hot-carrier energy loss rates →dE/dt↑ are evaluated through the Fröhlich– EPW formalism for carrier temperatures up to 5000 K. Applying +1% tensile strain to BaZrO3 collapses the dominant-mode electron–phonon coupling constant from ϑ = 1.31 to ϑ = 0.011, suppressing the hot-carrier cooling rate by more than 90% relative to the least favorable strain condition and yielding a thermalization time ϖtherm = 1,585 fs and a hot-carrier figure of merit FOMHC = 1,348 fs, surpassing all halide configurations by more than an order of magnitude. Landau polynomial fitting of ε2 min (ϱ) confirms that no strain-induced structural phase transition occurs within ±2% for any compound, establishing a safe phonon engineering window. Orbital-projected densities of states reveal two mechanistically distinct coupling classes: gap-closure-driven coupling in BaSnO3 and CsCaCl3 [Spearman correlation ς(Eg, ϑ) ↓ ↔0.70] and purely phonon-mode-softening-driven coupling in BaZrO3 and KTaO3 (ς ↗ +0.72), the latter being invisible to band structure analysis alone.

item.title: Characterizing the Hydrophobic Contribution to Adsorption on Ligand-functionalized Surfaces
item.description: The hydrophobicity of functionalized surfaces is critical, as these surfaces are widely used to modulate adsorption, self-assembly, fouling, and molecular recognition by controlling interfacial interactions with surrounding molecules. Despite their importance, characterizing the hydrophobicity of functionalized surfaces and quantifying its contribution to these phenomena remain challenging. Here, we use molecular dynamics simulations and enhanced sampling methods to quantify the hydrophobicity of surfaces functionalized with multimodal ligands, which can interact with solutes through multiple interaction modes. Specifically, we study a series of multimodal ligands grafted to these surfaces, including Nuvia cPrime, a commercially available glycine-based chromatography ligand, and its amino acid-derived analogs, which differ from it by additional chemical groups with systematically varied hydrophobicity. We quantify surface hydrophobicity from the free energy of removing interfacial water molecules and compare our results with ligand logP values, the solvent accessible surface areas (SASA) of ligand chemical groups, and protein-induced water displacement observed in molecular simulations. We then validate the relevance of the resulting hydrophobicity ordering using experimental protein binding trends. We find that water removal from small, localized regions centered on ligand clusters better captures adsorption-relevant surface hydrophobicity than removing water from the entire surface because these regions more closely represent proteinbinding sites. Additionally, we show that variations in ligand clustering across the same surface alter chemical group exposure, as indicated by SASA, resulting in spatial heterogeneity in surface hydrophobicity. Overall, this work provides a molecular-level approach for characterizing functionalized surface hydrophobicity and guiding the design of interfaces that control molecular adsorption.

item.title: Ipso-selective pyridine-to-aniline editing through amine-induced fragmentation
item.description: Skeletal editing enables the remodeling of aromatic frameworks, but pyridine-to-aniline conversions can generate multiple positional isomers, complicating analogue synthesis. Here we report an ipso-selective strategy that separates regiochemical control from diversification of the aniline nitrogen. Pyridines are converted through dearomatization and cycloaddition into stable, isolable bicyclic ketones, which undergo amine-induced condensation–fragmentation to afford anilines with the amino group positioned at the site corresponding to the original pyridine nitrogen. Both primary and secondary amines participate, enabling divergent synthesis from a common intermediate. Notably, regioisomeric intermediates derived from a 3-substituted pyridine converge to a single aniline product. The method also enables preparation of multiple analogues from a tropicamide-derived scaffold, illustrating the potential of this modular approach for medicinal-chemistry scaffold diversification.

item.title: Image-Charge Barriers, Not Polaron Kinetics, Limit Charge Extraction at Ligand-Passivated CsPbI3 Interfaces
item.description: Charge extraction across inorganic perovskite–organic ligand interfaces represents a critical materials bottleneck in perovskite optoelectronics, yet the defectindependent electrostatic origins of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we present a multiscale framework that combines first-principles density functional theory with macroscopic Scharfetter–Gummel drift-diffusion simulations to isolate and quantify this intrinsic transport barrier on CsPbI3 surfaces passivated by methylammonium (MA), butylammonium (BA), and phenethylammonium (PEA). We demonstrate that effective interfacial dielectric screening is governed by ligand orientational polarizability and adsorption geometry rather than isolated molecular polarizability, producing a counter-intuitive ordering εBA > εMA > εPEA that inverts the conventional molecular polarizability sequence. The resulting imagecharge barriers (Umax im = 202.6–229.8 meV) exceed kBT by nearly an order of magnitude, driving severe thermodynamic carrier depletion (CAF = 1.38 × 10−4–3.95 × 10−4), while all computed polaron reorganization energies (λ < 100 meV) confirm delocalized, large-polaron character—unambiguously establishing that the dominant bottleneck is electrostatic rather than kinetic. Despite its lowest electron reorganization energy (λe = 37.8 meV), PEA’s orientational locking generates the largest image-charge barrier (Umax im = 229.8 meV), whereas the conformationally flexible BA maximizes in-plane screening and reduces steady-state carrier accumulation by an order of magnitude under operational bias. Furthermore, ligand rigidity governs a structural electron–hole reorganization asymmetry (λh/λe = 0.98–1.85), establishing a defect-independent, purely structural mechanism for carrier selectivity. These findings deliver four quantitative design rules for charge-transparent passivation interlayers, replacing empirical ligand screening with a predictive framework anchored in orientational polarizability, adsorption geometry, and carrier-type symmetry. The identified image-charge barrier constitutes a Boltzmann activation energy Uim(T ) that is directly measurable via temperature-dependent photoconductance, providing an unambiguous experimental validation signature.

item.title: Reactive Machine-Learned Potentials Improve Predictions of Water Diffusion Behaviour in Defective Industrial Zeolite HY
item.description: Dealuminated HY (USY) zeolites are of major industrial catalytic importance, and the defects they contain, such as extraframework aluminum (EFAL) and silanol groups, strongly influence the behaviour of adsorbed species. Here, we show that reactive neural network-based machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) provide a substantial improvement in the simulation of water diffusion in these catalysts. They yield markedly improved agreement with quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) measurements of mobility for models of intact framework regions, refined further once EFAL and silanol defects are included explicitly, capturing the additional hindrance these sites impose on water motion. The ability of MLIPs to generate and stabilise realistic defect structures constitutes a step change in the molecular level and nanoscale modelling of industrial zeolites. This combined capability enables the quantitative investigation of defect-specific effects on nanoscale diffusion and provides a new approach for accurately modelling transport in industrially relevant zeolite catalysts.

item.title: A Direct-to-Biology Platform for Rapid Covalent Antibiotic Discovery
item.description: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacterial infections has created a critical need for new antibiotics. While natural product-based covalent antibiotic classes such as the β-lactams are highly effective, exploration of synthetic covalent antibiotics remains limited. Here, we present a direct-to-biology platform for covalent antibiotic discovery. Using tandem diazo transfer and copper-catalyzed azide-alkyne cycloaddition, we combinatorially synthesized 720 crude chloroacetamides within a matter of days and screened these for activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). By resynthesis and retesting, almost all hits were confirmed to be active, having potency profiles comparable to those of the initial screen. In situ chemoproteomic analyses revealed selective engagement of the essential enzyme HMG-CoA synthase by the most promising hits. We validated this target and obtained a co-crystal structure to better understand the binding mode of the compound. Altogether, this platform generates large libraries of covalently reactive compounds, identifies active compounds, and finds their molecular targets within a single screening campaign.

item.title: Development of oligo-thioester precursors for native chemical ligation of oligo-protein conjugates.
item.description: Protein-oligo conjugates have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality that unites the target-specificity and favorable pharmacokinetics of a protein carrier with the potency of an oligonucleotide payload. One challenge in the development of these biologics is that conjugation strategies often yield heterogeneous, high drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) products or require non-canonical amino acids and multi-step handling. Native chemical ligation (NCL) is a promising tool for protein-oligo conjugation, as the reaction is single-step and regiospecific to N-terminal cysteines, which can be genetically installed into proteins in a facile manner. However, methods for generating the required oligo-thioesters remain a technical challenge, especially when complex linker groups are desired. Here, we report an efficient protocol to generate four oligo linker-payloads (LPs) incorporating an anti-sense oligonucleotide targeting the MALAT1 gene, bis(2-sulfanylethyl)amine (NSS)- or thioacid-based thioester precursors, and diverse intervening linkers. The LPs were successfully ligated to an affibody and the crystallizable fragment (Fc) of an antibody, key protein carriers for protein-oligo therapeutics. The operationally simple, bespoke nature of this workflow enables the diversification of oligo payloads and linkers required for broad applications.

item.title: Structural and Spectroscopic Characterization of Californium Polyoxometalate Compounds
item.description: Californium (Cf3+) complexes with several Keggin-type polyoxometalate (POM) ligands have been synthesized and characterized, providing the first serial approach to Cf chemistry and a unique occasion to contrast its coordination properties with that of other felements. Contrary to trivalent lanthanides, americium and curium, californium yields a higher diversity of structures. Using microgram amounts of 249Cf, nine new structures containing Cf3+ have been obtained with the POM ligands [PW11O39]7-, [SiW11O39]8-, [GeW11O39]8-, and [BW11O39]9-, representing the largest series of Cf compounds ever isolated and significantly expanding experimental data on POM compounds with heavy actinides. Cf3+ crystallizes as the typical 8coordinate sandwich complexes with Keggin ions, [Cf(XW11O39)2]n-, but the long-range bond distances and twist angles of the Cf-POM complexes depart from any previous case reported. Comparative compounds obtained with the nearly isometric lanthanides also underline the uniqueness of the Cf3+ compounds beyond the ion size effects. The now extended family of [M(XW11O39)2]n- complexes also revealed previously unobserved topological isomers in such complexes, defined here as iota (ι) and omega (ω), with the Cf complexes’ isomerism often differing from the other f-elements. This first series of isotypic Cf compounds, CsyHz[Cf(XW11O39)2]·nH2O, (X = P5+, Si4+, Ge4+, or B3+), combined with structures previously obtained with Am3+, Cm3+, and lanthanides allows for the determination of bond valence sum (BVS) parameters for Cf3+ as well as the experimental determination of its 8-coordinate ionic radius: 1.066 ± 0.004 Å.

item.title: Analytical validation in catalytic CO2 conversion: Product identification, carbon accounting, and evidence for process performance
item.description: Reliably evaluating catalytic CO2 conversion requires distinct evidence for product identity, quantity, carbon origin, carbon accounting, and process performance. This critical narrative review compares those requirements across electrochemical, photocatalytic, and thermocatalytic conversion, with plasma-assisted hydrogenation as a methodological comparison. A five-step assessment traces the inference, alternative explanation, discriminating evidence, shared measurement dependencies, and remaining conclusion. Published cases distinguish product formation from carbon-source attribution, catalytic selectivity from carbon disposition, and repeatability from transferable performance. For a published plasma-only condition, subtraction and direct analysis differ by approximately 34 percentage points in methanol selectivity; differing collection windows limit attribution to one cause. Constructed calculations show how shared calibration and independent reactor uncertainty affect catalyst rankings differently, and how rankings can reverse when energy is expressed per recovered rather than formed product. The synthesis treats chromatography, quantitative NMR, isotope analysis, sampling recovery, flow measurement, and uncertainty as connected parts of the measurement procedure. The synthesis distinguishes contradictory evidence, insufficient experiments, and restricted source access. Priorities are independent tests of residual allocations, validation of representative collection pathways, matched operating intervals, and staged interlaboratory comparisons. The assessment is an applied interpretive procedure, not a validated scoring instrument.

item.title: Multifunctional Cellulose via Enzymatic Oxidation of Tripeptides
item.description: Cellulose is a natural, abundant and versatile biopolymer that has long been used in traditional applications such as paper and textiles and has gained interest in advanced applications including energy storage, healthcare, food, cosmetics, and coatings. For these applications, achieving robust functionality in cellulose nanocomposites remains a challenge due to poor control over the uniform distribution of added components. Here, we explore enzyme-activated tripeptides as versatile interfacial modifiers for introducing distinct functions into microbial cellulose. First, we demonstrate peptide-mediated formation of melanin-inspired coating with strong light absorption and potential UV-protective properties. Second, we demonstrate incorporation of graphene to create semi-conducting biocomposites. Microbial cellulose was exposed to the tripeptides KYF or KYW in the presence of tyrosinase, promoting peptide oxidation, assembly, and retention within the cellulose network. Pigmented coatings displayed a clear sequence dependence, with KYW exhibiting substantially greater adsorption and uniformity compared to KYF, which is consistent with additional hydrogen-bonding interactions provided by the tryptophan indole side chain and favorable carbohydrate–aromatic interactions that enhance cellulose affinity. In contrast, graphene incorporation was comparable for both peptides, suggesting that graphene immobilization is governed primarily by the general self-assembly of aromatic peptides rather than sequence-specific cellulose binding. The resulting composites showed uniform graphene dispersion, confirmed by optical and electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy, together with enhanced mechanical performance and electrical conductivity. These findings establish enzymatic peptide oxidation as a versatile strategy for introducing optical and electrical functionality into cellulose-based materials.

item.title: ChemConnect: Making chemical identifier relationships and disagreements explicit and actionable
item.description: Chemical identifiers serve as essential links between molecular structures, experimental measurements, biological activities, and regulatory information. Discrepancies can arise when independently curated databases assign different identifiers to the same substance, often due to curation inconsistencies or intentional differences in representing salts, solvates, protonation states, and stereochemistry. Here, we introduce ChemConnect, a provenanceaware graph framework designed to integrate chemical identifiers from NORMAN SusDat, EPA CompTox Chemicals Dashboard, and PubChem without resolving them to a single canonical chemical entity. The ChemConnect graph contains ∼8.5 million chemical identifier nodes and ∼7.5 million connections, of which ∼ 65 thousand are derived structural-parent and stereochemical relationships whose agreement with external references is systematically quantified. ChemConnect preserves the information supplied by each source and stores the derived relationships separately, so that users can see how each relationship was obtained. This allows users to compare sources, identify records whose identifiers contradict each other, and connect related records, such as a salt and its neutral form, that have no identifier in common.

item.title: Sm-Catalyzed Reductive Transformations of Enones
item.description: We report two Sm-catalyzed reductive transformations of enones. Using catalytic Sm(OTf)3 and Zn0 as the terminal reductant, Wieland–Miescher-type ketones underwent ring contraction to trans-hydrindanes bearing vicinal quaternary stereogenic centers. Under similar conditions but with 2-naphthalenethiol as a hydrogen atom donor, diastereoselective enone reduction outcompeted the ring contraction pathway, furnishing decalin products. The diastereoselectivity of the enone reduction was shown to be controlled primarily by the substrate structure; however, for certain substrates, the thiol structure could be used to improve the diastereoselectivity. Mechanistic investigation by cyclic voltammetry is also reported.

item.title: Proton-Gated Cobalt Catalysis Redirects Persistent Sulfinyl Radical Coupling toward Enantioselective C–S Bond Formation
item.description: The enantioselective construction of aliphatic C(sp3)–S stereocenters from alkyl radicals remains challenging. Persistent sulfinyl radicals are attractive partners for radical cross-coupling. However, their rapid diffusioncontrolled coupling with transient alkyl radicals provides limited opportunity for stereochemical discrimination. Here, we report a dual photoredox/cobalt catalytic system in which a Brønsted acid acts as a critical mechanistic gate, redirecting persistent sulfinyl radical coupling from a direct PRE-dominated pathway toward cobaltcontrolled enantioselective C–S bond formation. Mechanistic studies support reduction of Co(II) to Co(I) and subsequent formation of a Co(III)–H species in the presence of HX. Hydrogen-atom transfer between Co(III)–H and the sulfinyl radical generates RSOH, which subsequently associates with a chiral cobalt species to organize the sulfur center for stereoselective radical capture. The use of aprotic alkyl radical precursors, including alkyl trifluoroborates and trialkylboranes, decouples radical generation from proton availability and reveals the critical role of the Brønsted acid in stereocontrol. This method accommodates diverse alkyl radical precursors and enables a practical alkene hydroboration–sulfinylation cascade for the synthesis of enantioenriched sulfoxides.

item.title: Spin-Resolved Reaction-Network Exploration in AutoMeKin with Minimum-Energy-Crossing-Point Localization and an ⟨S2⟩ Single-Reference Check
item.description: Automated exploration of reaction networks typically assumes a single potential-energy surface. However, 3d transition-metal catalysis often involves two-state reactivity, where the rate-determining step may occur on a different spin surface. This work presents an open-source extension of AutoMeKin that incorporates spin considerations throughout. The extension features a GFN2-xTB exploration engine with spin-handling capabilities, identification of closely lying spin states, localization of minimum-energy-crossing-points (MECP) at relevant crossings, integration of MECP nodes connected by nonadiabatic edges within the reaction graph, nonadiabatic transition-state-theory rate calculations, and a multireference diagnostic based on ⟨S2⟩ to disable the single-determinant approach where it is not applicable. The extension is tested on three different iron systems. For H2CO and Fe(CO)5, blind path sampling was utilized, whereas targeted transition-state optimization was applied to the more complex cases. Subsequently, MECPs were localized without manual intervention for Fe(CO)5 and Tp-Fe(II)-ethyl, but not for the Fe(I) alkene-isomerization catalyst.

item.title: The Nuclear Landscape: A Five-Variable 3D-Printed Representation of the Nuclides
item.description: Traditional charts of the nuclides convey proton number, neutron number, and one other property (e.g. half-life or decay mode). We describe the design and fabrication of a modular three-dimensional model of the nuclides that encodes five nuclear properties. Proton number and neutron number determine planar position, half-life is represented by column height using a quantile-logarithmic transformation, decay mode is represented by colour, and year of discovery is represented by the area of the top of the column. The model provides a tactile and visual representation of >3400 nuclides with the stable nuclides forming the spine of the model. The digital models were made by an iterative human-artificial intelligence (AI) co-design workflow in which generative AI helped translate educational objectives and geometric constraints into 3D printable stereolithography (STL) files. Feedback from visitors to the completed piece was uniformly positive when describing their interaction and learning experience. Complete datasets, STL files, and representative design prompts are provided to facilitate reproduction and adaptation for educational use.

item.title: “NONO” calix[4]arene zirconium complexes with functionalized side chains
item.description: A series of zirconium (IV) complexes with a bis(N,N-Dimethylethylenediamino)-p-tert-butylcalix[4]arene, (L2H2), and (1S,2S)-N1,N1-Dimethyl-1,2-cyclohexanediamino -p-tert-butylcalix[4]arene, (L3H2), were synthetized and structurally characterized via single crystal X-ray diffraction and NMR. Comparing them with L1 complexes,1 slight increase in the stability towards protic substrates was observed as well as formal HCl elimination and formation of an anilino-anilido complex was observed for L3. Rac-lactide polymerization was attempted as well as intermolecular hydroamination of alkynes. The effect of the coordinating and basic side chains modifies the reactivity of the complexes but still do not show remarkable improvements in the catalytic applications.

item.title: Adsorption Free Energy of a Mobile Physisorbed Molecular Catalyst from Well-Tempered Metadynamics and from the Harmonic Approximation
item.description: The adsorption free energy of a molecular catalyst is usually calculated with harmonic frequency analysis of the optimized adsorbed structure, and errors are often blamed on anharmonicity. Here, using fac-Re(bpy)(CO)3Cl on graphene, we show that the main source of error is different. Harmonic analysis treats the complex as vibrating around a single minimum, but at 298 K, the complex can move across the surface, rotate around the surface normal, and rock. In this work, we use multiple-walker well-tempered metadynamics to sample the desorption coordinate and then convert the free-energy profile to a standard-state value, with the gas at 1 bar and the adsorbate at the standard surface concentration as recommended by Campbell et al. The result is ΔG°ads(298 K) = −64.1 ± 2.1 kJ mol−1 at PBE-D3(BJ), while the harmonic approximation gives −26.3 kJ mol−1. Of the 37.8 kJ mol−1 difference, only 1.7 kJ mol−1 comes from the anharmonic shape of the binding well along the surface normal; 36.3 kJ mol−1 is due to the frustrated translations and rotations of the bound complex, which the harmonic model treats as small vibrations around a single minimum. The two exceed the total by the 0.2 kJ mol−1 quantum-to-classical step, which acts in the opposite direction. Insertion-based estimators, which work well for small adsorbates in pores, do not apply here because the ensembles with and without the adsorbate–surface interaction are separated by 34 kBT and do not overlap. The missing entropy cancels out when comparing similar poses of the same adsorbate, but not when referencing the gas phase.

item.title: Taming the 8-Billion Parameter Model on a low-cost GPU card for Retrosynthesis
item.description: We explored the use of post-training quantization (PTQ) to enhance the efficiency of reasoning language models for chemical retrosynthesis in drug discovery. We specifically evaluated the RetroDFM-R model, demonstrating that reducing numerical precision to 4-bit significantly lowered GPU memory requirements while lowering Top-1 accuracy by only about 2 percentage points (3–4% relative) for NormalFloat-4 (nf4) and double-quantized nf4 (nf4dq). The accuracy for 8-bit quantization (int8_ao) was equivalent to the original model but reduced energy consumption by about 17% when only one prediction was required. By testing various quantization methods across different hardware configurations, the study revealed that these techniques allow complex chemical predictions to run on budget-friendly, consumer-grade GPUs. In the augmented setting the 4-bit models returned more distinct candidates, which raised Top-10 accuracy on the full test set by up to 0.8 percentage points; on reactions for which every model filled ten candidate positions, the original model remained the most accurate. In summary this study presents the first evaluation of PTQ applied to RetroDFM-R, a reasoning language model, for chemical retrosynthesis. Ultimately, the research suggests that quantization is a vital tool for making advanced chemoinformatics tools accessible to academic researchers who can run it on cards with smaller GPU memory and can reduce the energy per molecule by about 17 - 30% in the default setting, although it increases it by 30–35% in the augmented setting.

item.title: Machine-Learning-Guided Prediction and Statistical Analysis of Electronic Bandgaps in Double-Perovskite Oxides for Photovoltaic and Optoelectronic Design
item.description: Double-perovskite oxides (A2BB′O6) are attractive for photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications, but their bandgap depends on a compositional space too large for routine DFT screening. In this study, we build composition-only machine-learning models on 1,306 DFTcomputed (GLLB-SC) double perovskites, using 72 descriptors derived from elemental electronegativity, ionic/atomic radius, group and period position, Mendeleev number, and first ionization energy. Six regression algorithms were compared under 10-fold cross-validation where a tuned XGBoost model gave the best results (test R2 = 0.975, MAE = 0.188 eV, RMSE = 0.245 eV), outperforming all others with statistical confidence (Friedman χ2 = 45.14, p =1.4×10-7; Wilcoxon p < 0.005 throughout). SHAP analysis pointed to A-site group number and B-site electronegativity and radius as the main drivers of bandgap, matching the mechanisms reported in the original DFT study. These results demonstrate that interpretable, composition-only machinelearning models can reproduce DFT-level bandgap trends at negligible computational cost, providing a practical high-throughput screening tool for lead-free double-perovskite discovery.

item.title: SFEModeling.jl: multi-model, multi-curve fitting of supercritical fluid extraction kinetics with a graphical interface
item.description: SFEModeling.jl is an open-source Julia package for fitting kinetic models of supercritical fluid extraction (SFE) to experimental extraction curves. It implements the Sovóvá broken-and-intact-cells model, solved numerically along the extraction bed, together with a pseudo-steady-state shrinking core model and four empirical models (Esquível, Zeković, parallel kinetics, and a piecewise-linear spline). Several curves, each with any number of replicates, are fitted jointly. In the Sovóvá model the accessible-solute fraction xk/x0 is shared across curves while the mass-transfer coefficients are estimated per curve. Parameters are found by derivative-free global optimization, so no initial guesses are required. Data and operating conditions are entered in laboratory units, and results can be exported to text or Excel files. The same functionality is available from a browser-based graphical interface, distributed with a Windows installer and as a Julia app, so experimentalists can use the software without programming.

item.title: Selenium Alters the Tissue Distribution of Inorganic but Not Methylmercury in Zebrafish Larvae
item.description: Mercury toxicity is strongly influenced by its chemical speciation, with interactions between mercury and selenium species either mitigating or exacerbating toxic effects. Here, synchrotronbased X-ray fluorescence imaging was used to examine the influence of L-selenomethionine on the tissue distributions of inorganic mercury and methylmercury in zebrafish larvae. Inorganic mercury accumulated predominantly in the pronephric ducts and liver, whereas methylmercury was distributed more uniformly throughout the organism. Administration of L-selenomethionine substantially altered the distribution of inorganic mercury and increased selenium accumulation within the pronephric ducts. Subcellular-resolution imaging revealed strong spatial correlations among mercury, selenium, and sulfur following inorganic mercury exposure, revealing mercury-, selenium-, and sulfur-rich domains within the pronephric ducts. In contrast, L-selenomethionine had comparatively little influence on methylmercury distribution, although combined exposure increased tissue sulfur levels. These findings demonstrate fundamentally different interactions of selenium with inorganic and organometallic mercury species in vivo and emphasize the importance of both chemical form and subsequent metabolism in determining mercury–selenium interactions.

item.title: Polyoxometalate-controlled oxidative formation of bioinspired polydopamine hydrogels
item.description: Polyoxometalates (POMs) have been extensively explored as enzyme-mimetic catalysts capable of peroxidase-like peroxide-driven reactions. Specifically, transition metal-substituted POMs provide a molecular platform for tunable reactivity and kinetic control. Here, we use a titanium-doped Keggin polyoxomolybdate [(TiOH)PMo11O39]4- {TiOH} to crosslink a dopamine-functionalized alginate hydrogel in the presence of hydrogen peroxide under mild conditions which would otherwise prevent polymer formation. Tuning of the hydrogel rheological properties is possible by molecular-level reaction control. Experimental and theoretical studies are combined for comprehensive insight into the reaction mechanism of the catalytically active species.

item.title: A Readily Scalable Silylated Cyclic Allyl Sulfide Monomer for Degradable Vinyl Polymers
item.description: Introducing degradability into conventional vinyl polymers without sacrificing the versatility of radical polymerization remains a major challenge. Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization (rROP) is currently the most promising technique to impart degradability into vinyl-based polymers through the copolymerization of cyclic monomers with common vinyl monomers. However, among the various families of cyclic monomers reported to date, none simultaneously combines high efficiency, versatility, and compatibility with industrial-scale production. Here, we report a family of silylated cyclic allylic sulfides (CAS) designed to decouple radical ring-opening reactivity from post-polymerization cleavage. The representative monomer LC1 combines a CAS scaffold, which undergoes efficient radical addition–fragmentation, with an independently cleavable silyl ether linkage. LC1 is prepared in two steps from readily available precursors, and a simultaneous dual-feed strategy enables its facile and reproducible scale-up. LC1 displays monomer-dependent reactivity across several vinyl monomer families and introduces cleavable junctions throughout chain growth. Kinetic experiments, Mayo analysis and density functional theory reveal two distinct addition–fragmentation processes: rapid ring-opening incorporation of cyclic LC1 followed by a slower secondary transfer pathway involving the pendant allylic functionality generated after ring opening. The resulting polymers undergo backbone fragmentation under fluoride, acidic, basic and Lewis-acid conditions, with degradation kinetics further tunable through pH and silicon substitution. LC1 also remains compatible with emulsion polymerization and crosslinked networks, enabling chemically and thermally triggered disassembly of 3D-printed materials. Finally, in the context of upcycling, hydroxyl-terminated degradation fragments can be repurposed as polyol precursors for polyurethane network formation. This work establishes silylated CAS monomers as a versatile platform for independently programming radical polymer growth and material lifetime.

item.title: A Modular Continuous Flow Platform for Safe, On-demand Generation of HCF2N3 from R-22 Gas and Access to N-CF2H Triazoles
item.description: The N-CF2H motif recently emerges as a promising pharmacophore but modular and general strategy to access this scaffold remains scarce. Although difluoromethyl azide (HCF2N3) constitutes an ideal aminodifluoromethyl surrogate in this case, its exceptionally low ratio of C to N atoms (0.33), high volatility (b.p. = 8 oC), and heat/shock sensitivity render it particularly unsafe to handle and use in batch. On the other hand, R-22 (ClCF2H gas) is a phased-out refrigerent due to its ozone depletion potential and high global warming potential, and valorization of the reclaimed R-22 is highly desirable. Here, we report a modular continuous flow platform to efficiently enable a safe, on-demand generation of HCF2N3 from R-22 gas and its direct in-line utilization. Two HCF2N3 generation modules are developed to operate under aqueous or organic reaction conditions for accommodating diverse downstream reactions. The freshly generated HCF2N3 is immediately intercepted by downstream base-mediated or copper tube-catalyzed cycloadditions to yield a wide range of valuable N-CF2H triazoles using easily available alkynes, aldehydes and β-ketoesters. Our method completely circumvents isolation hazards, mass transfer limitations in batch, and enables previously improbable gas-to-gas transformation and multiphasic conditions.

item.title: Expanding Antibody-Drug Conjugates Mechanistic Diversity with Verubulin: A Dual Tubulin-Binding and Vascular-Disrupting Payload.
item.description: Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) have revolutionized targeted cancer therapy, yet their clinical success remains restricted by the limited diversity of cytotoxic payloads. Here we describe the development of verubulin as a novel ADC payload with a dual mechanism of action, combining tubulin inhibition with vascular disruption. Two successive ADC generations were designed and evaluated. First-generation conjugates used amide/carbamate linkage but were hampered by instability and modest efficacy. These limitations were addressed by a quaternarization approach, which delivered stable conjugates with subnanomolar, target-dependent cytotoxicity, and limited bystander activity. In vivo, these ADCs induced tumour regression with excellent tolerability and more durable tumour control than bevacizumab, the clinical reference for vascular disruption, although efficacy remained below benchmark ADCs T-DM1 and T-Dxd. These results support verubulin as a promising payload scaffold for next-generation ADCs.

item.title: Energy conserving variational dynamics with Gaussian wavepackets in the nonadiabatic regime
item.description: We present a theoretical framework for a “trajectory”-driven nonadiabatic dynamics, that generalizes the variational Gaussian wavepacket approach to dynamics on multiple diabatic states. By applying the time-dependent variational principle to a single Gaussian wavepacket per state, we obtain a set of coupled equations for the Gaussian center and width parameters that include terms arising from the coupling potential. We investigate the role of these terms as they change the Gaussian time-evolution, and of the initial conditions on the wavefunction for several standard benchmarks of nonadiabatic dynamics, including a three-state and a two-dimensional model. The state populations obtained with the fully variational Gaussian dynamics is found in close agreement with exact quantum results. Finally, we demonstrate that the use of Gaussian wavefunction in nonadiabatic dynamics preserves the symplecticity of the variational space, which ensures the energy conservation and minimization of error when solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.

item.title: Ordering-dependent subsurface reconfiguration reshapes the ORR activity ranking of L10 and L12 Pt–Fe nanoparticles
item.description: Nanoparticle catalyst properties are often governed by activation-induced subsurface reconfiguration and ordering-dependent structural responses rather than nominal bulk phases. Static idealized models therefore can miss the kinetic pathways that drive subsurface evolution and active-site redistribution during synthesis and activation. Here, we present an activation-mapped kinetic modeling workflow combining density functional theory (DFT), machine-learning cluster expansion (ML-CE), Metropolis Monte Carlo (MMC), and kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) to trace processing-driven structural evolution in L10 and L12 Pt–Fe nanoparticles. We define the activation-derived ensemble as the statistically sampled Pt-skin configurations generated by high-temperature ordering, selective Fe leaching, vacancy-mediated restructuring, and room-temperature activation. This ensemble construction links processing history to subsurface composition, surface morphology, and site-resolved catalytic response. Within the modeled activation sequence, phase-dependent Fe leaching produces an inversion in second-layer Fe enrichment relative to the ideal ordered references and changes the dominant active-site families, making L10-derived nanoparticles terrace-controlled, whereas L12-derived nanoparticles become comparatively edge-controlled. When coupled to steady-state *OH coverage kinetics, these activation-derived ensembles recover the experimental oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity ranking and reveal phase-specific size–activity trends missed by ideal models. More broadly, the results show that the activation-derived structures, rather than pristine phases alone, govern catalyst ranking and highlight how ordering-dependent subsurface reconfiguration can reshape static-model predictions.

item.title: What topology hold-out removes—and what it does not
item.description: Machine-learning screens of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture increasingly report the validation protocol that produced a score, and topology hold-out has become the standard stricter alternative to random splitting. Prior work already reads topology hold-out as a combined structural and chemical distribution shift; this work measures the size of the chemistry that the split withholds. On the hypothetical-MOF library hMOF (324,426 structures), 74.7% of coarse-grained chemical compositions occur in a single topology, accounting for 61.3% of structures, and seven of eleven topologies leave every structure without a chemical counterpart in training. On the one usable chemistry-matched pair (pcu ↔nbo), removing the partner topology raised nbo-side MAE by 70.0% while a size-matched control did not, and removing only the shared-composition partner rows improved pcu-side MAE, so partner coverage is direction-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial. A chemistry-key hold-out produces only 21.1% of the topology hold-out's R2 decrease, so the support loss is real but does not translate proportionally into performance loss. Across five independently redrawn 25,000-sample support sets, the top-1% hit rate fell from 50.4% to 19.3% under topology-grouped validation. A support audit in ARC-MOF, which is partly dependent on hMOF and uses different composition keys, confirms strong coupling under bounded sensitivity rather than as an independent replication. We retain topology hold-out as a stress test while recommending that groupedsplit reports disclose their chemical support, deployment-relevant aggregation and ranking performance.

item.title: Complete stabilization of surface oxygen vacancies in high-entropy oxides
item.description: High-entropy oxides retain a significantly larger population of oxygen vacancies (OVs) compared to their single-element or binary metal oxide counterparts, highlighting their unique potential as prospective electrocatalytic materials. However, the stabilization of surface oxygen vacancies (S-OVs) is highly challenging due to their inherently dynamic nature generally resulting in defect healing, migration, or initiation of structural collapse under operating conditions. By means of rational high-throughput materials science, we investigate the stability of S-OVs in (Cu-Fe-Ni-Cr-Zn)Ox high-entropy oxides covering a compositional search space of at least 5 to 35 %. A methodology based on X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and X-ray absorption spectroscopy is utilized to quantitatively follow the distribution of the OVs across the materials library. For low Zn stoichiometries, (Cu14-Fe13-Ni5-Cr8-Zn4)O55, complete stabilization of S-OVs is achieved even after prolonged exposure to ambient environment. The discovery of S-OV stabilization in our high-entropy oxide system is a prerequisite to exploit the unique properties of this class of materials for electrocatalytic applications and beyond.

item.title: Inhibition of Oxidative Activity by Photo-induced Surface Hydroxyl Groups in Bismuth Titanium Oxide Photocatalyst Detected by Single-Molecule Fluorescence Imaging
item.description: The surface structure of semiconductor photocatalysts plays a critical role in the extraction of charge carriers during photocatalytic reactions. However, the surface structures of many photocatalysts are dynamic under catalytic conditions, which makes identifying photo-induced changes and their effect on photocatalytic activity challenging. Herein we use super-resolution, single-molecule fluorescence imaging to map the spatial distribution of catalytically active regions and quantify the changes in activity of those regions for photocatalytic oxidation in bismuth titanium oxide (Bi4Ti3O12) nanoplates. Individual nanoplates varied widely in both activity and stability, reflecting significant heterogeneity among a single synthesis batch of photocatalyst particles. We observed that while the nanoplates are more active around the perimeter of the basal facet, those perimeter regions decrease in activity at the same relative rate as the rest of the basal facet, indicating a spatially uniform degradation mechanism. Through ensemble structural characterization of the nanoplates after irradiation, we identified surface hydroxyl groups as the photo-induced feature. Our results indicate that surface hydroxyl groups introduce hole trap states that increase charge recombination at the surface of the nanoplates leading to the observed decrease in activity. Surprisingly, we identified nanoscale features that do not begin with high activity but exhibit a slower rate of activity loss, leading to regions with greater activity relative to the rest of the basal facet at the end of imaging. Our findings highlight the importance of not only understanding how different nanoscale features influence catalytic activity but also how these features evolve over time, which dictates catalyst stability.

item.title: AI-driven design of a novel synthetic route to malaria drug ganaplacide
item.description: Malaria is a deadly infectious disease that disproportionately affects low- and middle-income countries. Ganaplacide is a drug candidate that is highly effective against malaria, and the ability to produce it at low cost is essential. Here we show how we used a combination of AI-driven design and expert chemistry knowledge to develop a novel synthetic route to ganaplacide. The AI retrosynthesis algorithm suggested a non-evident two-steps synthesis of the imidazolopiperazine core of the molecule from benzyl-protected dimethylpiperazinone through a strategic thioimidate intermediate. We also present the Synthetic Confidence Score, which assesses the level of risk associated with a given retrosynthetic disconnection and allows balancing creativity and reliability. The synergy between AI creativity, metrics such as the Synthetic Confidence Score and expert chemist knowledge has the potential to unlock non-evident efficient routes for important molecules, when expert chemists alone have explored mainstream chemistry unsuccessfully.

item.title: Bead-Spring Model Analysis of Linear Viscoelasticity for Unentangled Multi-Cyclic Polystyrene Melts
item.description: Multi-cyclic (MC) polymers, in which multiple ring units are connected within a single molecule, are expected to exhibit properties distinct from those of linear and trivial ring polymers. Here, we performed graph-theory-based bead-spring model calculations for a series of unentangled MC polystyrene (MC-PS) melts with different chain connectivities and compared the results with previously reported experimental linear viscoelastic data. This calculation allows for the comparison of linear viscoelasticity among different MC molecules using a single, architecture-independent time-scale. The distribution and multiplicity of the eigenvalues λp at mode number p, which determine the relaxation times through τp ∝ 1/λp, of the MC molecules depends strongly on the architecture and its overall symmetry. In addition, the model reasonably captured the experimental linear rheological behavior of the MC-PS melts, including the complex modulus G*(ω) and the zero-shear viscosity η0, although the experimental data have modest differences. Furthermore, we found that the architecture dependence of η0 can be semi-quantitatively organized using the squared radius of gyration calculated from the bead-spring model, Rg,BS2, rather than relying only on the number of constrained segments, ncs, which has been used as an empirical architectural parameter in previous studies. This descriptor also distinguishes MC architectures with the same ncs but different rheological responses, demonstrating that chain connectivity provides a physically grounded basis for describing the linear viscoelasticity of unentangled MC polymer melts.

item.title: Antisolvent precipitation of Zinc Porphyrin Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks Enables J-Aggregation Mediated Electrochemiluminescence for Synthetic Cannabinoid Sensing
item.description: Zinc porphyrin hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (ZnTCPP HOFs) represent attractive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) luminophores; however, their tendency to undergo uncontrolled short-range π–π stacking at solid/liquid interfaces induces aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) and severely limits the ECL efficiency. Existing strategies for suppressing ACQ rely mainly on covalent or coordination-mediated ligand engineering and often require laborious multi-step synthesis. From the perspective of colloid and interface science, we herein report a chitosan (CS)–DMF antisolvent precipitation strategy that reorganizes the interfacial hydrogen-bond network between CS and the carboxyl groups of ZnTCPP HOFs, enabling a controlled transformation of bulk crystals into short-range aggregates with local J-type coupling. Such synergistic colloidal-interface regulation suppresses short-range π–π stacking while enabling J-aggregates to enhance the ECL emission, boosting the peak ECL intensity without the need for an additional co-reaction promoter. On this basis, an aptamer-based ECL sensor was constructed for the ultrasensitive detection of the synthetic cannabinoid 5F-EDMB-PINACA, achieving a limit of detection of 8.61 × 10⁻16 g/L together with satisfactory selectivity and reliable determination in e-cigarette liquid samples. These findings demonstrate that colloidal-interface regulation provides an efficient and synthesis-free route toward high-performance ECL sensing.

item.title: Conformational and Tautomeric Effects on the excited-states of Sulfonated Azo Dyes
item.description: In this work, we present a systematic investigation of the ground- and excited-states of six anionic sulfonated azo dyes with broad applications in the textile industry: Allura Red, Amaranth, Carmoisine, Ponceau, Red 2G, and Sunset Yellow. Ground-state properties were evaluated using density functional theory (DFT) at the $\omega$B97X-D4/ma-def2-SVP level of theory. To identify the most suitable functional for excited-state calculations and to assess vertical excitation energies to low-lying excited-states, we tested a series of hybrid, meta-hybrid, and range-separated hybrid functionals from Jacob's ladder using the Tamm-Dancoff approximation (TDA) and the ma-def2-SVP basis set and compared to results from RI-CC2 and STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD approaches. excited-state properties were then further examined using TDA at the CAM-B3LYP//$\omega$B97X-D4/ma-def2-SVP level of theory. Additionally, the quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) was applied to explore density-related properties in both ground and excited-states. We found, perhaps not surprisingly, that excitation weakens the \ce{N=N} bond in both the enol and keto forms of the dyes, but with variations depending on the molecule, conformer, and electronic state.

item.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
item.description: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.

item.title: Toward Interpretable Graph-Based Machine Learning for Combustion Kinetic Model Generation
item.description: This work presents an atom-conserving and interpretable graph neural network (GNN) for combustion kinetic model generation, where atoms are represented as nodes, covalent bonds are represented as edges, and reactions are represented as bond-rearrangement operations. Its artificial-intelligence (AI) contribution is a reaction generator that extends a standard Graph Isomorphism Network with Edges (GINE) architecture through reaction-context embeddings, reaction branching & third-body reaction inputs, Arrhenius-rate-parameter prediction, pairwise decoding, and stochastic inference over evolving reactant pools. Trained on the Li–Dryer hydrogen combustion kinetic model (8 species and 21 reactions), the GNN reproduces trained chemistry and generates element-balanced new reactions and intermediate species outside the training dataset, many of which have experimental analogues. When trained on a subset of the Li–Dryer dataset, the model recovered most held-out reactions and revealed relationships between samples (reactions) in the model’s latent space. The results suggest that the model learns transferable local reaction structures and generates valid species and reactions. As with any reaction generators, the generated reaction models require thermochemical and kinetic verification; the intended engineering application is low-cost reaction-pathway exploration for new fuels and prioritization of experiments and first-principles calculations to develop new combustion kinetic models.

item.title: A Readily Scalable Silylated Cyclic Allyl Sulfide Monomer for Degradable Vinyl Polymers
item.description: Introducing degradability into conventional vinyl polymers without sacrificing the versatility of radical polymerization remains a major challenge. Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization (rROP) is currently the most promising technique to impart degradability into vinyl-based polymers through the copolymerization of cyclic monomers with common vinyl monomers. However, among the various families of cyclic monomers reported to date, none simultaneously combines high efficiency, versatility, and compatibility with industrial-scale production. Here, we report a family of silylated cyclic allylic sulfides (CAS) designed to decouple radical ring-opening reactivity from post-polymerization cleavage. The representative monomer LC1 combines a CAS scaffold, which undergoes efficient radical addition–fragmentation, with an independently cleavable silyl ether linkage. LC1 is prepared in two steps from readily available precursors, and a simultaneous dual-feed strategy enables its facile and reproducible scale-up. LC1 displays monomer-dependent reactivity across several vinyl monomer families and introduces cleavable junctions throughout chain growth. Kinetic experiments, Mayo analysis and density functional theory reveal two distinct addition–fragmentation processes: rapid ring-opening incorporation of cyclic LC1 followed by a slower secondary transfer pathway involving the pendant allylic functionality generated after ring opening. The resulting polymers undergo backbone fragmentation under fluoride, acidic, basic and Lewis-acid conditions, with degradation kinetics further tunable through pH and silicon substitution. LC1 also remains compatible with emulsion polymerization and crosslinked networks, enabling chemically and thermally triggered disassembly of 3D-printed materials. Finally, in the context of upcycling, hydroxyl-terminated degradation fragments can be repurposed as polyol precursors for polyurethane network formation. This work establishes silylated CAS monomers as a versatile platform for independently programming radical polymer growth and material lifetime.

item.title: Structural evolution of the P2-Na2/3Ni1/3Mn2/3O2 sodium-ion battery cathode material resolved by 3D electron diffraction
item.description: P2-Na2/3Ni1/3Mn2/3O2 is a promising cathode for sodium-ion batteries, yet its electrochemical behavior is governed by a complex sequence of structural transformations whose microscopic origins remain poorly understood. In particular, Na+/vacancy ordering is expected to play a central role in the phase evolution but is challenging to resolve using powder diffraction alone. Here, we combine continuous-rotation 3D electron diffraction (3D-ED) with operando and ex situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) to establish a comprehensive structural picture of NaxNi1/3Mn2/3O2 across the full electrochemical window (1.0 V – 4.5 V). 3D-ED resolves Na+/vacancy ordering in sub-micrometer crystallites, revealing ordered P2 structures at Nax = 2/3, 1/2, and 1/3. In each case, Na+/vacancy ordering lowers the symmetry of the parent P2 framework and produces arrangements that minimize electrostatic repulsion while satisfying Pauling’s second rule. Transient phases at Nax = 3/5 and 2/5 are also observed during charging, while two highly sodiated P2 phases are accessed by discharging to low voltages. At high states of charge, extensive Na+ removal drives the P2→O2 transition and produces pronounced stacking disorder, demonstrating that the layer glide is not fully coherent. Bond-valence analysis further tracks transition-metal charge compensation during Na+ extraction. Together, these results establish Na+/vacancy ordering as a key structural variable governing phase stability, charge compensation, and structural transformations in P2-Na2/3Ni1/3Mn2/3O2, while highlighting 3D-ED as a powerful approach for resolving complex ordering phenomena in battery materials.

item.title: Tailoring Gas Transport Properties in MOF-Based Mixed Matrix Membranes: The Role of Filler Morphology and Surface Functionalization
item.description: The development of high‑performance mixed‑matrix membranes (MMMs) for gas separations relies on precise control of filler morphology and optimized polymer–filler interactions. In this study, we elucidate how crystal size, morphology, and surface functionalization of the perfluorinated metal-organic framework (MOF) F4_MIL‑140A(Ce) influence the gas transport properties of MMMs based on Pebax® 1657 and Matrimid® 9725 matrices. Through systematic modulation of reaction conditions, we synthesized sub‑micrometric F4_MIL‑140A(Ce) particles with tailored size and aspect ratio, achieving improved dispersion and interfacial contact within the polymer phases.
