A post‑synthetic grafting strategy using stearic acid further enhanced the compatibility of the MOF without altering crystallinity, pore accessibility, or CO2 adsorption behavior, as confirmed by powder X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and sorption analyses. MMMs prepared with the surface-functionalized MOF displayed improved polymer–filler adhesion, minimized interfacial voids, and significantly enhanced gas transport properties. In particular, the Pebax® 1657-based MMMs approached the 2008 Robeson upper bound for CO2/N2 separation, driven primarily by increased CO2 solubility. In contrast, Matrimid® 9725 MMMs exhibited substantial improvements in H2/N2 and O2/N2 selectivity, linked to enhanced diffusivity. The insights presented in this work provide a rational framework for engineering MOF–polymer interfaces and advancing membrane‑based gas separation and CO2 capture technologies.

item.title: Cerium Photoredox-Catalyzed Ring Expansion of Cyclic Allylic Alcohols
item.description: Medium-sized aliphatic rings are underrepresented in drug discovery despite their advantageous balance of rigidity and flexibility. Existing synthetic limitations hinder broader exploration of this valuable chemical space. This work presents a general and efficient method for the one- and two-carbon ring expansion of 5- and 6-membered allylic alcohols to larger cyclic ketones using cerium-based photoredox catalysis. Employing ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) activation, a dual catalytic system featuring Ce(OTf)3 and 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA) enables selective generation of alkoxyl radicals under mild conditions. A hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalyst, (TRIPS)2, is critical for productive C–C bond formation and radical termination. The method tolerates various nitrogen-protecting groups, vinyl substitutions, and ring systems, including bridged and fused frameworks, affording 7- and 8-membered ketones in moderate to excellent yields (38–98%). Notably, expansion to challenging [5.2.1] bicyclic and fused benzannulated scaffolds is demonstrated. This strategy offers a divergent and synthetically accessible route to sp3-rich, conformationally diverse drug-like scaffolds from simple precursors.

item.title: Enthalpy-Driven Design Rules for Multi-Shell Multimetallic Nanoparticles
item.description: Multimetallic nanoparticles (NPs) offer access to a vast compositional and architectural design space, yet controlled formation of core-shell and multi-shell architectures rapidly becomes unpredictable as compositional complexity increases. As a result, architectural outcomes are often regarded as system-specific and governed primarily by kinetic effects. Here, we identify a unifying thermodynamic principle that governs shell formation in multimetallic NPs based on binary mixing enthalpies and phase behaviour. By systematically establishing enthalpy-driven rules in binary NPs and extending them to higher-order compositions, we show that elemental segregation and the composition and sequence of multiple shells in NPs containing up to five elements are predictable despite their combinatorial complexity, even when synthesised in a simple one-pot wet-chemical reaction. These results demonstrate that thermodynamic interactions maintain predictive power as compositional complexity increases and provide a general framework for rationalising architectural design in multimetallic NPs.

item.title: Catalytic N-Cbz Deprotection of Amino Acids and Dipeptides over Spherical SiliaCat Pd(0)
item.description: Investigation of hydrogenolytic removal of N-benzyloxycarbonyl (N-Cbz) protecting groups from amino acid and dipeptide derivatives mediated by spherical SiliaCat Pd(0) under mild conditions using an H2-filled balloon allowed to optimize reaction parameters including solvent composition, substrate concentration, Pd loading, temperature, and catalyst particle size. The spherical catalyst enabled efficient N-Cbz deprotection at Pd loadings as low as 0.25–0.50 mol% under selected conditions, with high conversions, isolated yields, and selectivities across a broad range of amino acid derivatives. The methodology was successfully extended to N-Cbz-protected dipeptides, although substrate-specific optimization of solvent composition and Pd loading was required for more challenging substrates. Catalyst particle size primarily influenced reaction kinetics, with smaller particles providing faster deprotection, and larger particles advantageous for packed-bed continuous-flow applications. The catalyst showed useful chemoselectivity in the presence of Boc and tert-butyl ester protecting groups, while selective N-Cbz removal in the presence of benzyl esters could be achieved through appropriate control of reaction conditions. Comparison with commercial heterogeneous Pd catalysts showed that the spherical organosilica catalyst provided a favorable combination of complete conversion, high isolated yields, and consistently low Pd leaching. Overall, these results establish spherical SiliaCat Pd(0) as a practical, non-pyrophoric, and versatile heterogeneous catalyst for N-Cbz deprotection of amino acid and dipeptide derivatives, supporting its application in peptide-oriented synthesis.

item.title: Artificial Cells with a Cytoskeleton from Synthetic Self-Replicating Molecules
item.description: Living cells couple molecular replication and cytoskeletal assembly to changes in shape and mechanical stability, but reconstructing this relationship in synthetic compartments remains challenging. Here, we confine self-replicating supramolecular fibers within giant polymer lipid hybrid vesicle-based artificial cells. Seeded replicator growth produces luminal fiber networks and deforms the surrounding membrane into spindle-like morphologies, with fiber and membrane interactions controlled by membrane composition and fiber glycation. Covalent crosslinking of the fiber network within the lumen enables the artificial cells to withstand cellular aggregation during prolonged co-culture. The stabilized artificial cells remain incorporated within HepaRG cell-based microtissues for 28 days while the surrounding cells differentiate into hepatocyte- and biliary-like phenotypes. These results establish a chemical route by which assembly-driven replicators within a compartment can generate cytoskeletal

item.title: Water-Model Dependence of Absolute Binding Free Energies across the Bromodomain Family
item.description: The choice of explicit water model may affect absolute binding free energy (ABFE) predictions for bromodomains, whose conserved acetyl-lysine pockets contain structured waters. We assembled a benchmark of ten distinct bromodomain–ligand complexes with experimental isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamics and compared four TIP-family water models, TIP3P, TIP4P, TIP5P, and TIP7P, using a common alchemical protocol. TIP3P gave the lowest point-estimate mean unsigned error (MUE), 1.56 kcal mol−1, against 1.89–2.11 kcal mol−1 for the other models, at the lowest cost. TIP7P correlated best with experiment (r = 0.73), but the experimental affinities span only 2.1 kcal mol−1, about the size of the errors of the models. The 0.55 kcal mol−1 MUE difference between TIP3P and TIP7P had a nominal 95% paired bootstrap interval that excluded zero when only the benchmark composition was resampled, but not when the calculated affinities were perturbed by their sampling-sensitivity measures or the four charged ligands were left out. No other paired difference was resolved, including after finite-size corrections for the charged ligands. The leg decomposition shows that solvent and complex contributions can compensate, so water-model effects must be judged over the complete binding cycle. With one calculation per complex and model, the higher-site TIP models gave no demonstrated accuracy benefit with this force field for 1.4–2.7 times the cost.

item.title: Rigor & Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Best Practices for Kinetic Studies
item.description: Kinetic measurements can support or falsify mechanistic hypotheses in electrocatalysis, but only when rates reflect intrinsic catalytic behavior and models separate kinetic information from experimental artifacts and interfacial complexity. This perspective presents best practices for acquiring and interpreting electrocatalytic kinetic data, including mitigating artifacts arising from transport, ohmic losses, catalyst restructuring, contamination, and incomplete product accounting. Similarly, we provide guidelines for constructing rate expressions that treat elementary charge transfer, adsorption, and surface coverage, which enable interpretation of kinetic observables like apparent transfer coefficients, rate orders, and apparent activation energies that reflect properties of an interconnected reaction network. Mechanistic conclusions are strongest when competing hypotheses are tested against multiple complementary observables, including spectroscopy, isotopic labeling, and theory, enabling meaningful and reproducible mechanistic comparisons across laboratories.

item.title: Gold-Mediated Cascade Cyclization on-route to the Total Synthesis of (−)‑Presilphiperfolan-1-ol
item.description: We report a concise and convergent total synthesis of (−)-presilphiperfolan-1-ol, a highly strained tricyclic sesquiterpene bearing five contiguous stereocenters. Central to our strategy is a gold(I)-catalyzed cascade cyclization of a silyl enol ether containing an enyne motif, which simultaneously constructs the fused tricyclo[5.3.1.04,8]undecane core and sets three remote stereocenters. A systematic ligand screening revealed that, in contrast to prior reports, both NHC-type ligands and bulky Buchwald-type phosphines promoted exclusive 5-exo-dig cyclization, indicating a strong substrate-controlled preference that overrides steric and electronic ligand effects. The full sequence proceeds in nine steps from commercially available materials, and the key cyclization step was successfully scaled up to the gram scale. Access to enantioenriched material was achieved via a stereoselective methylcuprate addition catalyzed by a chiral NHC-Ag complex. This work establishes a practical and modular strategy for the synthesis of complex terpenoids and offers new mechanistic insight into ligand-substrate interplay in gold-catalyzed enyne cyclizations.

item.title: Second-generation tau PET tracer in situ binding assessed with fluorescence imaging
item.description: Brain positron emission tomography (PET) imaging is a valuable tool which allows visualization of the pathological structures inside the living patients’ brains. While amyloid-β PET tracers have been in use with Alzheimer’s disease patients in clinics, tau PET tracers have still not entered the clinical routine. Second-generation tau PET tracers have been developed with the aim to overcome the limitations of the first-generation tau PET tracers, such as low sensitivity and off-target binding. However, the detailed pathological characterization of these tracers’ binding is still needed for fully understanding their potential as accurate markers of pathogenic tau. Herein, we focused on the second-generation tau PET tracer Genentech Tau Probe 1 ([18F]GTP1) and made use of the fluorescent properties of its non-radioactive unlabeled variant GTP1 for correlative fluorescence microscopy. The results show that GTP1 binds to tau tangles and neuropil threads (NPTs), but not amyloid-β plaques. Importantly, our results indicate that there is a strong correlation between the fluorescent GTP1 signal and the [18F]GTP1 signal detected with autoradiography, which is currently the standard way of studying the tau PET tracer binding in situ. Together, this data shows the robust application of a non-radioactive tau PET tracer in binding studies in post-mortem tissue and sheds new light on the tau binding properties of GTP1.

item.title: Methyl-Induced Hydrophobicity and Electronically Tuned Copper Nanocluster COF for Highly Selective Nitrate to Ammonia Electrosynthesis
item.description: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (eNO3-RR) offers a promising route for sustainable ammonia production while mitigating nitrate pollution. Yet high NH3 selectivity remains challenging owing to proton-coupled multi-electron transfer pathways and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, we report a trinuclear Cu nanocluster-based covalent organic framework (CuMePh) featuring methylfunctionalized π-conjugated extended porous framework that provides a molecular-level strategy for modifying the interfacial wettability and electronic environment of the catalytic framework. Benefiting from this modulation strategy, CuMePh exhibits a maximum faradaic efficiency (FE) of 98% for nitrate to ammonia conversion, with an NH3 production rate of 2161 μg h-1 cm-2 (5402.5 μg h-1 mg-1 cat.) at -0.5 V versus RHE under the investigated alkaline conditions. Compared with the non-methylated CuPh analogue, CuMePh also exhibits a higher water contact angle. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the electronenriched Cu3-cluster nodes in CuMePh facilitate nitrate activation and sequential hydrogenation by lowering the free-energy requirement and optimizing intermediates binding, while simultaneously suppressing the competing HER. This work highlights a molecular-level design principle that couples electronic-structure engineering with interfacial-property regulation in nanocluster-based COFs, offering new opportunities for developing highly selective electrocatalysts for sustainable nitrogen-cycle transformations.

item.title: Programming of Dissipative Networks and Transient Vesicles Using Intrinsic Kinetic Discrimination of Thiol Oxidation
item.description: Programmable dissipative systems that mimic life’s ability to execute timed functions—such as apoptosis triggered by inherent reactivity contrasts—remain a fundamental challenge, as most synthetic designs lack the kinetic complexity to orchestrate multi-step, autonomous sequences. Here, we introduce a synthetic dissipative network in which the intrinsic oxidation kinetics of mono- and dithiols serve as an embedded reaction window to program a cascade of thiol-thioester exchange reactions. This autonomous mechanism dictates reaction timing and sequence, translating molecular-scale kinetic differences into a programmed, system-level response. By extending this principle to the material scale, we further construct fuel-driven, self-assembled vesicles that undergo a life-like cycle of formation, functional execution (as catalytic microreactors), and dissipation. This work establishes intrinsic kinetic hierarchies as a general design paradigm for programming temporal order in non-equilibrium systems, inspiring the development of time-evolving functional materials.

item.title: Influence of Divalent Cations on the Mechanical Properties of DNA Origami Six-Helix Bundles
item.description: The mechanical behavior of DNA origami nanostructures (DONs) is governed by both design parameters and ionic environment, yet their coupled effects remain poorly understood. Here, atomic force microscopy (AFM)-based contour analysis is used to quantify the persistence length (Lp), contour length (Lc), and end-to-end distance (Ree) of DON six-helix bundles (6HBs) with different staple crossover densities. Non-ligated and ligated 6HBs are compared in the presence of MgCl2 and SrCl2, while oxDNA simulations employing implicit monovalent salt screening help distinguish design-dependent from ion-specific effects. While providing comparable diffuse electrostatic screening, Mg2+ and Sr2+ interact differently with DONs and produce distinct design-dependent mechanical responses. For non-ligated 6HBs, lower Lp values are obtained in Sr2+ than in Mg2+, with the magnitude of the difference depending on crossover density. Paired Ree-versus-Lc analysis further indicates greater bending heterogeneity in Sr2+. In the presence of both cations, ligation may lead to an increase or a decrease in Lp depending on crossover density. Simulations reproduce the opposite ligation responses of the two designs but not the Mg2+-associated behavior, supporting an additional contribution from specific divalent cation interactions. These results establish crossover density, backbone continuity, and cation species as coupled variables whose interplay controls DON mechanics.

item.title: Improved Prediction of Mössbauer Quadrupole Splitting at High and Low Temperatures with a Quantum Chemical Ensemble Approach
item.description: Mössbauer spectroscopy is a key method for characterizing the electronic structures of iron compounds. The resulting Mössbauer parameters show a well-established temperature dependence. For quantum chemical calculations that are often used to aid in the interpretation of Mössbauer spectra, this poses a major challenge: they commonly employ a single, rigid equilibrium structure that is assumed to deliver good results for low temperatures up to ca. 80 K. In this work, we reveal this approach to be a rather severe approximation. We use a structural sampling approach that captures the effect of temperature dependent molecular vibrations on the quadrupole splitting. Even for low temperatures, this approach delivers a significantly improved agreement with experimental data. In addition, the T-dependence of the quadrupole splitting can be qualitatively reproduced for four iron(II) high spin complexes. The results are analyzed in terms of the individual EFG tensor contributions, which shows the origin of the temperature dependence being rooted in different electronic structures with varying contributions at different temperatures. Limitations in the sampling approach and electronic structure method are discussed. The approach presented herein may provide better agreement with experiment in future in situ and operando studies at low, ambient and elevated temperatures.

item.title: Charge-Transfer-State Descriptors from Donor–Acceptor Interfaces Enable Improved Prediction of Indoor Organic Photovoltaic Efficiency
item.description: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) devices have attracted significant attention as lightweight, flexible, and solution-processable alternatives to conventional solar cells. In this work, a novel computational workflow was developed to generate donor–acceptor interfacial adducts for non-fullerene acceptor (NFA)-based indoor OPV systems and to investigate their charge-transfer (CT) characteristics using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations. Molecular docking followed by excited-state analysis enabled identification of important CT descriptors, including excitation energies, electron–hole separation, participation ratios, and charge-transfer characteristics. A dataset containing 30 donor–acceptor pairs were subsequently constructed by combining these CT descriptors with molecular fingerprints and frontier molecular orbital (FMO) parameters. Machine learning (ML) models based on ElasticNet and XGBoost algorithms were then trained to predict OPV power conversion efficiency (PCE). Our results demonstrate that incorporating physically meaningful CT descriptors derived from donor–acceptor interfaces significantly improve the ML-based prediction of OPV efficiencies from a small dataset.

item.title: A Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operator Framework for Zero-Plating Fast Charging of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Real-Time Electrochemical State Estimation and Barrier-Riding Optimal Control
item.description: Extreme fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is critically limited by internal lithium plating at the negative electrode-separator interface, driving rapid degradation and thermal hazards. Real-time mitigation is fundamentally impeded because the interfacial plating overpotential (ηplating) is inaccessible to non-invasive sensors, leaving conventional protocols blind to metallic lithium deposition. While high-fidelity Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) models resolve these dynamics, their computational cost (∼ 8 s) precludes embedded closed-loop control, whereas empirical equivalent circuit models lack the spatial resolution to detect plating. To resolve this trade-off, we develop a physics-informed 1D Fourier Neural Operator (FNO-1D) surrogate incorporating an explicit cumulative charge integral Q(t) = ∫ I dt to preserve mass conservation. Trained on 7,771 continuum DFN trajectories, the surrogate achieves a 4, 349× speedup (1.84 ms inference) with high fidelity (VRMSE = 5.40 mV, ηplating, RMSE = 2.24 mV). Coupled with an Ensemble Smoother with Multiple Data Assimilation (ESMDA), the framework filters sensor noise (±10 mV to 5.94 mV) and reconstructs unobservable plating dynamics (RMSE = 4.12 mV, 95% CI = ±3.22 mV), establishing continuous closed-loop observability. A Barrier-Riding Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) policy then maximizes charging current along the degradation boundary. Across a 10% - 80% SOC window, it cuts charging time by 21.7% (33.7 min vs. 43.0 min CC-CV)while strictly preventing lithium plating (ηplating ≥ +14.81 mV > +5.0 mV), limiting peak temperature to 38.5◦C, and decreasing SEI growth by 21.5%. Finally, transferability is experimentally validated across two phys ical cycler benchmarks: cross-chemistry transfer on Oxford pouch cells, and chemistry-matched validation on commercial RWTH Aachen Sanyo 18650 NMCcells, achieving a terminal voltage tracking RMSE of 33.02 mV (86.0% error reduction over zero-shot transfer) providing an experimentally grounded paradigm for degradation-free fast charging.

item.title: Synthesis of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural using sulfonated calix[4]arene in brine and rapid reaction monitoring with micellar capillary electrokinetic chromatography
item.description: The acid-catalyzed dehydration of D-(−)-fructose into 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) and side product levulinic acid (LA) in saturated aqueous sodium chloride was investigated with 1H quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (qNMR) and micellar capillary electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC). The highest isolated HMF yield of 32.7 ± 5.4 % was obtained with 2 mol% sulfonated calix[4]arene (sC4A) from 0.3 M fructose over 4 hours at 140 °C showing modestly improved performance over p-toluenesulfonic acid, methanesulfonic acid, p-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid, sulfuric acid and hydrochloric acid. Host-guest interactions between sC4A and HMF were investigated with 1H NMR titrations at different temperatures revealing supramolecular complexation at 30 °C, whereas p-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid bearing same functional groups but lacking the macrocyclic cavity of sC4A did not show interactions with HMF. A MECK method for the HMF analysis from acidic reaction mixtures was developed reaching limit of detection and limit of quantification values of 0.003 mM and 0.009 mM, respectively. Here we demonstrate that MEKC can be used to track the production of HMF at the concentration range 0.1–10 mM within a total analysis time of 2 minutes.

item.title: Electrochemically-driven dynamic surface chemistry breaks the selectivity-conversion tradeoff in the oxidative coupling of methane
item.description: The partial oxidation of methane to C2 products such as ethylene (C2H4) and ethane (C2H6) is a notoriously challenging catalytic reaction since the key properties, namely the C2 selectivity and CH4 conversion, scale inversely with each other. Despite decades of research on catalyst design, this fundamental C2 selectivity-CH4 conversion tradeoff remains a preeminent challenge.1 While traditional thermochemical catalyst design approaches seem inadequate to surmount said challenge, the electrochemical oxidative coupling of methane (EOCM) presents an alternative approach to enhance catalytic performance by dynamically altering the working state of the catalyst. In this study, we use (La, Sr)1-xTiO3±δ as a model system to demonstrate how electrochemistry enables one to dynamically tune the surface chemistry for enhancing C2 selectivity. Depending on the bulk composition, we observe either step changes in C2 selectivity or even a continuously increasing C2 selectivity trend by using La0.24Sr0.60TiO3-δ: this composition, once electrochemically activated, can break the traditional OCM tradeoff. We demonstrate that any C2 selectivity enhancement effects are determined by the surface La/Ti and Sr/Ti ratios which dynamically evolve under electrocatalytic conditions. The enrichment of La at these surfaces is central to enhanced C2 selectivity values and is crucially modulated by both the initial surface and bulk composition. The results presented herein highlight the potential of electrochemical materials activation for overcoming traditional challenges in partial methane oxidation and provide guidance on materials design for maximizing the C2 selectivity of EOCM.

item.title: Carbonyl Recycling Limits Productive Ethanol Formation during Syngas Conversion on Rh(211): A First-Principles Microkinetic Analysis
item.description: Higher alcohol synthesis from syngas on Rh involves a highly branched and reversible reaction network in which formation of a C–C bond does not necessarily lead to a higher-alcohol product. Here, a thermodynamically consistent first-principles mean-field microkinetic model is used to determine how carbon is partitioned among methane, methanol, ethanol, and higher-carbon intermediates on Rh(211). Across a 100-point temperature–pressure domain, increasing turnover progressively favors methane and methanol over ethanol. CO insertion provides the dominant entry into the C₂ carbonyl pathway. However, 79–94% of this carbonyl flux is subsequently returned to C₁ species through the C–C bond scission of CH₃CO* to CH₃* + CO*, a process referred to here as carbonyl recycling. Consequently, the principal C–C-forming reactions carry substantial flux but have relatively small degree-of-rate-control coefficients for ethanol production. Instead, hydrogenation of ethoxy to adsorbed ethanol becomes increasingly rate controlling, while methane formation and oxygen-removal chemistry strongly influence ethanol productivity. CHO insertion contributes productively at low activity but carries net reverse flux at high activity, showing that a low forward activation barrier alone does not determine the steady-state direction of a reaction. Methanol provides an additional competing sink for oxygenated C₁ carbon. Within the present Rh(211) reaction network, higher-alcohol formation therefore depends not only on forming C–C bonds but also on preventing newly formed C₂ intermediates from returning to C₁ species before they are converted to ethanol.

item.title: Mapping How Ligands Shape Spin-State Thermodynamics in Fe(II)N6 Complexes: Insights from the SCO ATLAS
Fluoroalkynes: The Last Frontier of Organofluorine Chemistry?
item.description: Molecules containing carbon-fluorine bonds are of global importance in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and polymers and are widely studied. However, little is known about fluoroalkynes where a fluorine atom is directly bonded to a carbon atom that forms part of a carbon-carbon triple bond. Pioneering studies in the 20th century established that these compounds are typically unstable, but their chemistry has remained largely unexplored to date. Here, we outline methods to prepare a diverse range of fluoroalkynes for the first time, rationalize the reasons behind their low stability, and demonstrate six different classes of reactions of fluoroalkynes and their difluorocyclobutadiene dimers.

item.title: Copper-Catalyzed Asymmetric Remote ε-Arylation/Cyclization of Yne-Indole Esters with 5-Aminopyrazoles toward Polycyclic Fused Seven-Membered Azaheterocycles
item.description: Chiral Cu-catalyzed asymmetric remote ε-arylation/cyclization of yne-indole esters with 5-aminopyrazoles is reported to construct polycyclic fused seven-membered azaheterocycles. After systematic screening of copper sources, chiral ligands, bases and temperature protocols, the optimized CuCl2/L12/DABCO system delivers products in good yields and high enantioselectivities. This transformation exhibits broad substrate compatibility, and steric/electronic effects on stereocontrol are discussed.

item.title: High-Valent Copper(III) Cyanide Tetramer Stabilized by Trifluoromethyl Ligands and its Multifaceted Reactivity
item.description: High-valent neutral copper(III) complexes are highly elusive species with strong Lewis acidic properties and high effective nuclear charge. Herein, an unprecedented copper(III) cyanide [Cu(CF3)2(CN)]4 stabilized in a tetrameric square-like scaffold with bridging cyanide ligands was isolated and fully characterized in the form of tetrahydrate [Cu(CF3)2(CN)(H2O)]4, including X-ray crystallography. This tetrameric scaffold is stable to Lewis bases, while the apical ligands easily undergo substitution to acetonitrile and cis-trans isomerization in the presence of acetone. Lewis acidity of copper(III) cyanides – hypothetical Cu(CF3)2(CN) and a tetrameric scaffold [Cu(CF3)2(CN)]4 – was evaluated by experimental and computational methods. Relevance of the [Cu(CF3)2(CN)(solv)]4 scaffold for carbon-carbon bond formation was demonstrated by spontaneous reductive elimination of CF3CN at room temperature in high yield, and trifluoromethylation of a boronic acid.

item.title: Phosphorus-Mediated Optical Defect Engineering in Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes
item.description: Defect engineering of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) offers a versatile strategy for tailoring their optical properties through localized chemical modification. However, expanding the range of accessible defect chemistries beyond established oxygen- and aryl-based functionalities remains an important challenge. Here, we report a straightforward, light-driven strategy for introducing phosphorus-derived defects into (6,5)-enriched SWCNTs using triphenylphosphine (TPP) and a photosensitizing dye. Ultraviolet irradiation in the presence of TPP and eosin Y generates a new near-infrared emission feature centered at 1125 nm, assigned to a defect-associated emissive state (E11*), alongside the intrinsic nanotube emission at 997 nm. The formation of this state depends on the TPP concentration, photosensitizer concentration, and irradiation time, and is accompanied by attenuation of the intrinsic optical transition and an increase in the Raman D/G intensity ratio, indicating progressive structural modification of the nanotube framework. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals a phosphorus-associated chemical state and changes in the carbon chemical environment, supporting phosphorus incorporation and the formation of modified carbon sites. Control experiments further demonstrate that defect formation requires both photosensitization and irradiation, is enhanced under oxygen-depleted conditions, and is suppressed by radical scavenging, consistent with a radical-mediated photochemical pathway. Complementary density functional theory calculations support the formation of a covalent carbon–phosphorus bond, accompanied by a change in phosphorus coordination from three- to four-coordinate, and reveal a phosphorus-associated electronic trap state near the valence-band edge. These findings establish phosphorus-mediated defect engineering as a complementary approach to tailoring SWCNT optical properties and provide a foundation for investigating the relationships between defect chemistry, localized electronic states, and near-infrared emission.

item.title: Non-Markovian Memory Kernels in Condensed-Phase Chemical Dynamics: From Dipole Dephasing and Conical Intersections to Spin Crossover and Radical-Pair Magnetoreception
item.description: Standard theoretical formulations of ultrafast condensed-phase molecular processes rely heavily on Markovian master equations and time-local Lindblad semigroups that assume memoryless bath relaxation (t ≫ τB). However, in viscous solvents, structured protein binding pockets, and biomolecular matrices, environmental fluctuations exhibit power-law algebraic memory tails K(t) ∝ t−µ (µ ∈ (0, 1)) where Markovian approximations break down. In this work, we develop an analytical and computational framework for non-Markovian chemical dynamics governed by the causal Caputo fractional memory kernel of the Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation (MEUWE). We apply this framework across five benchmark regimes of contemporary chemical physics. First, in molecular dipole autocorrelation dynamics, fractional dephasing replaces exponential Markovian damping with Mittag-Leffler decay Eµ (−Γ0 τ0µ tµ), extending the 10% electronic coherence lifetime by 13.40× (134.15 fs vs. 10.01 fs in H2), while coupled-channel Volterra equations achieve a benchmark vertical excitation mean absolute error (MAE) of 37.85 meV across pyscf Full Configuration Interaction (FCI) benchmarks with exact zero self-interaction error on one-electron ions (0.00 meV vs. TD-B3LYP 1884.37 meV). Second, at the 2D two-state conical intersection governing ultrafast rhodopsin retinal photoisomerization, viscoelastic solvent memory generates a +24.75 fs delay in non-adiabatic transition onset while suppressing coherent recoil back-transfer by up to 99.7% and preserving an all-trans photoproduct quantum yield of 62.625%. Third, in avian cryptochrome magnetoreception, fractional sub-Ohmic spin-bath relaxation delays singlet-triplet dephasing, producing an anisotropic magnetic compass contrast gain of 11.27× (and up to 266.94× at low fields) relative to standard exponential models. Fourth, in [Fe(bpy)3]2+ spin crossover, exact Stieltjes–Laplace inversion yields an asymmetric Fuoss–Kirkwood distribution of relaxation lifetimes spanning 2.288 decades of full-width at half-maximum (FWHM). Finally, on chemical reaction barriers, fractional Grote–Hynes transmission theory predicts a non-monotonic Kramers turnover with enhanced dynamic barrier transmission κGH = 0.513620 (vs. Markovian Kramers 0.242536). These results establish a unified, non-Markovian foundation for condensed-phase photochemistry, quantum biology, and barrier-crossing kinetics.

item.title: PerMix: Algorithmic Pathway Planning for Multicomponent Halide Perovskite Synthesis
item.description: The reproducible growth of multicomponent halide perovskite single crystals depends critically on the stoichiometry of the precursor solution: even small deviations introduced during weighing or dissolution can change phase purity, defect density, and the lattice parameters of the resulting crystals. Today, recipes for such systems are still planned largely by hand in spreadsheets, which are error-prone, difficult to audit, and impractical for the compositional spaces of multicomponent solid solutions. We present PerMix, an open-source Python framework that formalizes precursor planning as a constrained mass-balance problem and solves it transparently. The stoichiometric model, the combinatorial enumeration of precursor pathways based on a rigid/flexible partition of cations, tolerance-based validation, deduplication of identical salt formulations, deterministic ranking of pathways, geometric stability indicators (Goldschmidt tolerance and octahedral factors), and the SQLite reference database are described in full, with every governing equation stated explicitly. The tool was used to grow nine (MA1−xCsx)Pb(Br1−zYz)3 (Y = Cl, I) single crystals by antisolvent vapor-assisted crystallization; X-ray diffraction shows the systematic lattice expansion and contraction expected from the nominal substitutions. We also discuss the limits of the approach explicitly: precursor stoichiometry does not account for ion segregation, and quantitative composition analysis as well as homogeneity profiling are identified as future work.

item.title: An [Fe32] molecular metal oxide
item.description: Reaction of [Fe16] with 3-chloropyridine results in formation of an [Fe32] cluster, whose magnetic skeleton describes interwoven triangular and square tilings, demonstrating that pre-formed molecular iron oxides can be used as starting materials to access new species. Magnetic measurements reveal competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions, resulting in significant spin frustration.

item.title: VHH-Bench: A Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Nanobody–Antigen Complex Predictions Across CDR3 Conformations
item.description: Accurate prediction of nanobody–antigen complex structures is critical for the development of diagnostic, therapeutic and biosensing applications. However, progress in this area have been constrained by the limited availability of experimentally determined nanobody–antigen complex structures. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled highly accurate prediction of protein structures and protein-protein complexes, yet accurate modelling of nanobody–antigen interactions remains challenging due to the diverse binding modes exhibited by nanobodies. Here, we present VHH‑Bench, a benchmarking workflow for the systematic evaluation of nanobody–antigen complex structure prediction methods. We curated a non-redundant dataset of experimentally resolved nanobody–antigen complexes and evaluated six state-of-the-art models: AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, ESMFold2, HelixFold3 and Protenix-v2. Complexes were stratified according to CDR3 conformation, enabling separate assessment of kinked and extended nanobody classes. Prediction performance varied substantially between models and conformational classes. Protenix-v2 achieved the highest overall docking accuracy, success rate and proportion of high-quality predictions, with its advantage most pronounced for nanobodies with extended CDR3 conformations. In contrast, all evaluated models showed reduced accuracy and higher failure rates for complexes containing kinked nanobodies. While increased stochastic sampling provided slight improvements in some cases, its overall impact was limited and did not substantially affect the relative performance ranking of the evaluated models. VHH-Bench provides an extensible and reproducible benchmarking workflow for standardised dataset curation, nanobody classification, model evaluation and confidence analysis, facilitating the rigorous assessment and future development of nanobody–antigen complex prediction methods. The VHH-Bench framework is available at https://github.com/haiboyugroup/VHH-Bench.

item.title: Precursor Formulation Redirects Phase Competition and Thermal Evolution in Silver Multinary Chalcogenide Ag-M-Ch (M = Zr, Cr, Sn, Sb) Nanocrystals
item.description: Multinary nanocrystal synthesis requires chemically dissimilar metals to enter a common framework while competing with binary crystallization and metal reduction. We examine this competition through 31 preparation records spanning nominal Ag8SnS6, Ag4Zr3S8, AgZrSe2, AgCrSe2, and Ag3SbS3 targets in an oleylamine–octadecene platform. In a matched Ag–Zr–S comparison at 240 °C for 20 min, replacing an elemental-sulfur-derived stock with trioctylphosphine sulfide redirects a dense diffraction fingerprint toward a sparse fcc-Ag-compatible series. Comparison with independently identified crystallographic records further reveals substantial overlap of the sulfide and selenide fingerprints with acanthite Ag2S and published metastable P21/n Ag2Se, respectively. Microscopy resolves condition-dependent morphology, local lattice order, and elemental association within selected fields. Calorimetric heating and cooling traces reveal preparation-dependent responses, with ten individually resolved higher-temperature events at 88.63–176.33 °C. Annealing at 300 °C for 2 h under Ar yields composition-dependent morphological endpoints; two interpretable diffraction pairs distinguish persistence of an Ag-compatible component from redistribution of a more complex Ag–Sb–S fingerprint. The results identify precursor formulation as a control over competing crystalline pathways and show why thermal sensitivity must be interpreted in the context of those pathways. This comparative library connects reaction design with structural discrimination and subsequent processing response in silver-containing chalcogenides.

item.title: Homogeneous–Heterogeneous Hybrid Oxidation Catalysis Based on Multiple Adsorption Enabling Efficient Aerobic Amide Oxygenation
item.description: Homogeneous–heterogeneous combined catalysts, such as immobilized homogeneous catalysts and single-atom catalysts (SACs), have been developed to improve catalytic performance and practicality and elucidate catalytic mechanisms. However, achieving new catalytic functions beyond those of the individual components remains challenging. Homogeneous–heterogeneous hybrid catalysis offers a contrasting approach: homogeneous catalysts can coordinate/adsorb onto heterogeneous catalysts, allowing the two components to cooperate and potentially enable new catalytic processes for efficient molecular transformations. Nevertheless, reports of such hybrid catalysis remain limited, particularly for oxidation catalysis. We achieved effective homogeneous–heterogeneous hybrid oxidation catalysis by adsorbing a homogeneous phthalimide N-oxyl (PINO) radical catalyst onto a supported heterogeneous Pd nano-(hydr)oxide catalyst, enabling efficient aerobic α-oxygenation of structurally diverse amides (up to 99% yield; 15 examples). This hybrid oxidation system also accommodated amides that possess α-C–H bonds with high bond dissociation energies and are challenging substrates for previously reported amide α-oxygenation systems, including those involving direct hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) by PINO. Comprehensive characterization, control experiments, kinetic studies, and detailed comparisons with Co-catalyzed systems and Pd SACs support that the hybrid radical species formed on the Pd nano-(hydr)oxide surface through PINO adsorption efficiently facilitate HAT of amides via their coadsorption at nearby Pd sites.

item.title: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF AROMATICITY IN TAUTOMERIC EQUILIBRIA
item.description: Tautomerism, the interconversion of small molecules via proton and π-electron shifts, poses a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as different tautomers can exhibit distinct physicochemical properties and receptor-binding profiles, while computational approaches have been widely applied to predict tautomeric equilibria, most methods often overlook electronic properties such as aromaticity, which are critical to molecular stability. Here, we explore the role of aromaticity in tautomeric equilibria using a computational framework that integrates density functional theory (DFT) calculations with interpretable machine learning (ML) models. Aromaticity, which is challenging to measure experimentally, is quantified via Harmonics Oscillator Model of Aromaticity (HOMA) values and incorporated as a molecular descriptor. To enhance interpretability, we employ shallow ML models and assess feature contributions both intrinsically and using post-hoc explainability techniques. Our results demonstrate that both intrinsic and post hoc feature importance approaches capture similar trends associated with aromaticity. This highlights the complex influence of aromaticity on tautomeric equilibria and suggest that ML models, when combined with quantum-mechanics-based descriptors and explainable feature analyses, could be applied more broadly to capture important trends in other physicochemical properties beyond tautomer stability.

item.title: HF· · ·H2S Hydrogen-Bonded Clusters as a Model for Probing Subtle Cooperative Effects
item.description: Hydrogen-bond (HB) cooperativity is usually analysed for whole networks, and its variation between individual HBs is poorly understood when strong and weak donors coexist. We resolve 126 HBs in 20 neutral cyclic (HF)m(H2S)n clusters (Nmon = m + n = 3–7). The molecular tailoring approach (MTA) at the MP2/aug-ccpVTZ level splits each in-cluster HB energy into an isolated-dimer part and a network-associated (cooperative) part. The mean MTA energies of the F–H· · ·F, F–H· · · S, S–H· · · F and S–H· · · S bonds are 9.03, 8.47, 2.57 and 2.45 kcal mol−1, respectively. The cooperative part averages 2.11 kcal mol−1 per HB and is positive for nearly all HBs. In these structures, it correlates more strongly with HF content than with cluster size and changes little beyond five monomers. The cooperativity gain index, the cooperative part divided by the isolated-dimer energy, identifies fluorine-accepting HBs as the most enhanced, and S–H· · · F bonds stand out among the weakly bound dimers. For HF-donor HBs, the MTA energy correlates strongly with the H· · ·A distance and the electron density at the bond critical point. By the criteria of the quantum theory of atoms in molecules, these HBs are medium-strength interactions with partial covalent character, whereas the H2S-donor HBs are weak closed-shell interactions that local descriptors predict less well. The HB-resolved energies provide reference data for testing interaction models and machine-learning potentials; applying them to atmospheric or astrochemical systems requires further work.

item.title: Chemoselective Copper(l)-Catalyzed 1,2-Reduction of Conjugated Amides by a Molecular Recognition Strategy
item.description: The selective 1,2-reduction of conjugated amides represents an elusive transformation, owing to the intrinsically low reactivity of the amide group and competing conjugate reduction. Here, we report an unprecedented copper(I)-catalyzed hydrogenation of conjugated amides that selectively furnishes allylic alcohols using molecular hydrogen as the terminal reductant. A bifunctional copper catalyst exploits molecular recognition of a privileged amide motif to enable reduction of the amide functionality while preserving the conjugated alkene, thereby reversing the chemoselectivity commonly associated with copper hydride catalysis. The method provides access to a range of aromatic, heteroaromatic, aliphatic, and conformationally restricted allylic alcohols and tolerates additional reducible functionalities. Mechanistic studies reveal a decisive interplay between base-mediated E/Z isomerization and selective recognition and hydrogenation of the E-configured substrate. Moreover, isolation of a conjugated aldehyde intermediate supports a stepwise pathway involving amide reduction, C–N bond cleavage, and subsequent aldehyde hydrogenation. These results establish molecular recognition as a strategy to unlock otherwise inaccessible chemoselectivity in catalytic hydrogenation.

item.title: A Broadly Deployable Method for Repeated Hyperpolarized 13C Metabolic Imaging in Living Animals
item.description: Hyperpolarized 13C-MRI enables real-time imaging of metabolic conversions in vivo, but remains largely restricted to specialized sites with superconducting high-field MRI and polarization infrastructure. Here we present a broadly deployable method for preclinical hyperpolarized 13C-metabolic imaging, which combines signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE), a parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization technique, with detection of [1-13C]pyruvate-d3 in a compact 436 mT permanent-magnet small-animal MRI system. SABRE yields 13C-pyruvate polarization of 13% at ~30 mM in a purified, biocompatible solution, with a T1 relaxation time of 140 s. In a transgenic breast cancer mouse model, 13C-chemical shift imaging after injection resolves pyruvate, pyruvate hydrate and lactate in vivo, maps elevated lactate-to-pyruvate ratios in mammary tumors and images three freshly prepared pyruvate doses sequentially in the same animal in less than one hour. This compact SABRE-to-low-field method makes repeated hyperpolarized 13C-metabolic imaging mobile and accessible in standard preclinical research environments.

item.title: Hydroxyurea synthesis using resonant acoustic mixing in ethanol
item.description: Hydroxyurea derivatives have important medicinal utility acting as enzyme inhibitors and anticancer agents. Their syntheses have, however, entailed low yielding routes employing long reaction times and toxic reagents such as phosgene. Towards sustainable and environmentally benign hydroxyurea synthesis, a one-step hydroxycarbamoylation approach is described employing resonant acoustic mixing (RAM) to expedite reactions at higher concentration. Eighteen medicinally relevant hydroxyurea were synthesized in 68-91% yields using ethanol as green solvent.

item.title: Adsorption–Absorption Polymer Purification (AAPP): A Mass Transfer Strategy for Removing Residual Monomer from Synthetic Polymers
item.description: After polymerization, synthetic polymers frequently contain residual monomers, solvents, and other low molar mass compounds that can adversely affect material properties and subsequent applications. Their removal remains challenging, as conventional purification methods such as precipitation and dialysis are often time-consuming, difficult to standardize, and generate substantial amounts of solvent waste. Herein, an Adsorption–Absorption Polymer Purification (AAPP) method that combines a polymer immobilization through physisorption with a selective extraction of the corresponding residual monomer (or compounds) into a nonsolvent phase is introduced. Model polymers were employed to evaluate the performance of AAPP and to identify suitable operating conditions. Quantitative proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H NMR) demonstrated near-complete removal of residual monomers within comparatively short purification times while preserving the molecular characteristics of the polymers. Furthermore, the purified polymers were recovered in high yields and successfully employed as precursors for subsequent block copolymer syntheses, confirming the retention of their functionality. It is also demonstrated that AAPP can be efficiently utilized for, at least, the multigram scale production of specialty polymers. These results demonstrate that AAPP provides an effective and versatile strategy for polymer purification and highlight the potential of coupling absorption and adsorption to mitigate transport limitations in purification processes.

item.title: GVIM 2.0: A Multi-Agent Research System for Chemistry and Materials Science
item.description: Large language models are increasingly used as natural-language interfaces for chemistry and materials research, but their utility in scientific workflows depends on their ability to connect user requests with executable tools, structured data handling, and verifiable outputs. Here, we present GVIM 2.0, a multi-agent research system designed to support computational and informatics workflows in chemistry and materials science. GVIM 2.0 integrates language-model-based task planning with domain-specific Skills, packagebacked computational tools, sandboxed execution, and artifact generation. On a 400-question public benchmark suite spanning ChemBench, MaScQA, and ChemLLMBench, the complete GVIM 2.0 workflow answered 325/400 questions correctly, achieving an accuracy of 81.25%, compared with 285/400 questions and 71.25% accuracy for a same-base API-only baseline. We further evaluated GVIM 2.0 on task-native workflows covering molecular solubility prediction, steel yield-strength prediction, reaction-table extraction, MS/MS spectral retrieval, chemical entity extraction, retrospective BACE inhibitor prioritization, Matbench experimental band-gap modelling, and temporal external validation of BACE1 activity prediction. These workflows generated inspectable outputs, including prediction files, metrics, figures, and reports. The results show that GVIM 2.0 can organize reproducible data-to-result workflows for selected chemistry and materials informatics tasks, providing a practical framework for tool-augmented scientific research assistance.

item.title: Resolving Ultrafast Carrier-to-Exciton Conversion in CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals Formed from Solid-State Photochemistry
item.description: Photoinduced conversion provides an alternative pathway to form CsPbBr3 nanocrystals from their twodimensional analogues, nanoplatelets, using optical excitation in the solid phase. Although this transformation has been previously observed, it is unclear how the ultrafast dynamics of excitons in the resulting nanocrystals compare with those of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals synthesized in solution. In this study, we used femtosecond pump-probe spectroscopy to monitor the photoinduced conversion of n = 2 CsPbBr3 nanoplatelets in real time and investigate the charge carrier dynamics of the resulting nanocrystals. To investigate the processes that dominate the excited-state dynamics, we performed excitation-density-dependent pump-probe measurements and analyzed the transient kinetics using singular value decomposition methods. From this analysis, we identified two characteristic decay associated spectra connected to charge carrier cooling following photoexcitation. Comparison of these spectra with literature reports indicates that nanocrystals generated through photoinduced conversion exhibited carrier relaxation pathways similar to those of CsPbBr3 nanocrystals prepared by conventional colloidal synthesis. Our results provide insight into the ultrafast photophysics of photoinduced CsPbBr3 nanocrystals and established a connection between their formation through photoinduced conversion in the solid-state and the excited-state dynamics of similar materials synthesized through conventional solution-phase methods.

item.title: Wigner Momentum Estimation and Sampling with Local Modes: A Second-Moment Approximation to High-Frequency Momentum Marginals
item.description: Instantaneous local Gaussian approximations assign nuclear momentum widths from the curvature of the potential at each sampled configuration. Strongly compressed bonds can consequently acquire large momentum widths even when their positions are drawn from an anharmonic path-integral ensemble. We estimate momentum covariances from pathintegral coordinates and forces in local modes that follow molecular deformations. These covariances define Gaussian approximations to high-frequency Wigner momentum marginals without evaluating a Hessian at each configuration. The resulting sampling recovers the Maxwell momentum distribution in the classical limit. A rotating bond model with harmonic stretching and periodic torsion agrees with an independent quantum reference within statistical uncertainty. For trans-azobenzene at 300 K with 32 beads, the most compressed C–H bond receives a mass-weighted momentum variance of 36.53 kJ mol−1 from LGA and 19.55 kJ mol−1 from the local covariance along the same physical stretch direction. Temporal holdout errors in C–H second moments are 7.2–7.6%, compared with 2.2–5.1% for LGA relative to the finite-bead reference; the demonstrated benefit concerns the suppression of local width spikes. The largest collective C–H width remains sensitive to estimator noise. These results support the method as an approximation to high-frequency momentum widths without a frequency cap. Position-conditioned quantum correlations, non-Gaussian tails, and the continuum-bead molecular limit remain outside the demonstrated accuracy.

item.title: Deterministic Preparation of Intermolecular Spin States Through Collective Light Emission in Copper Porphyrin Aggregates
item.description: The coupling of electron spins in open shell systems drives formation of distinct singlet and triplet states whose transitions possess unique coherence properties relative to those of doublets. Here we show that exchange interactions couple the electron spins on neighboring Cu cations within porphyrins macrocycles that participate in aggregate formation. Following photoexcitation, we find a ‘low field’ EPR signal whose peak position and shape are reproduced by simulations of anti-ferromagnetically coupled electron spins. We use time-resolved light emission and EPR results to propose that this ‘low field’ peak appears due to a singlet to triplet transition that results in selective, deterministic population of the lowest energy state in the coupled spin system. Our results highlight how enhanced radiative relaxation in molecular aggregates ligated with open shell transition metal cations can be used to design the coupled spin states that participate in EPR transitions. This design principle could be used to further extend the use of molecular chromophores in quantum information science and technology applications.

item.title: Predicting excess solvation in binary solvents toward green organic semiconductor processing
item.description: Replacing halogenated solvents in organic semiconductor inks benefits from binary mixtures that balance dissolution and film drying, yet mixing changes solvation beyond the pure-solvent contributions. Here, we introduce ShellEx, a three-dimensional contact-shell model distilled from openCOSMO-RS that predicts this endpoint-fixed excess solvation from force-field geometries. Trained on 10,640 calculated curves for aromatic cores resembling organic semiconductors, ShellEx reduces the error by 27% on held-out curves relative to a zero-excess reference, which interpolates linearly between pure-solvent free energies. On 148 measured curves of eight solutes, its error, averaged with equal weight per solute, is similar to that of openCOSMO-RS and below that of simpler baselines. An openCOSMO-RS map of 200 solvent pairs for 35 cores ranks limonene–γ-valerolactone first among six predefined candidate-green pairs, with a median 1.35-fold concentration gain over the zero-excess reference. ShellEx selects the same pair and reproduces the pair ranking with a Spearman correlation of 0.85. ShellEx thus offers a route to prioritize green binary solvent pairs and compositions for halogen-free organic semiconductor inks before experimental testing.

item.title: Interstitial Oxygen and a Two-Dimensional Migration Pathway in Mo-Substituted Palmierite Ba3V2−xMoxO8+x/2
item.description: Palmierite oxides are promising oxide-ion conductors, with conductivities exceeding those of related hexagonal perovskite derivatives. However, aliovalent Mo6+ substitution in Ba3V2O8 has previously been demonstrated only at high substitution levels. Here, the Ba3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.3) was investigated using X-ray and neutron powder diffraction, 51V and 17O solid-state NMR spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT), and bond-valence site-energy (BVSE) calculations. Combined Rietveld refinement reveals that Mo6+ substitution introduces a charge-compensating interstitial oxygen site (O3) at x = 0.3, transforming isolated (V, Mo)O4 tetrahedra into corner-sharing polyhedra with mixed coordination. DFT-supported 17O NMR identifies additional oxygen environments associated with Mo in four- and five-fold coordination, suggesting oxygen bridges between adjacent MoO5 polyhedra. 51V NMR confirms predominantly tetrahedral vanadium coordination, alongside a minority V environment , distorted by occupation of a nearby O3 site. BVSE calculations indicate that O3 bridges neighboring polyhedra in the abplane, enabling a low-barrier, two-dimensional oxide-ion migration pathway involving apical O1 and interstitial O3 sites. These findings establish interstitial oxygen incorporation as the key structural mechanism facilitating low-barrier two-dimensional oxide-ion transport at low Mo substitution levels in the palmierite family, with broader implications for hexagonal perovskite ionic conductors.

item.title: Imbalanced burner heat release for enhanced ethylene yield in industrial-scale cracking furnaces
item.description: Symmetric burner arrangements with uniform heat release are the default design for cracking furnaces. However, the present study reveals that this symmetric layout leads to inferior heating conditions and reduced ethylene yields in specific coils. Therefore, an imbalanced heating strategy is proposed: side burners are grouped by location, with the fuel flow rate of Group L set to four times that of Group R while maintaining the same total fuel consumption. This approach increases the heat load on the disadvantaged coils by up to 2.65% and boosts their ethylene yields by nearly 10%, improving the overall average yield by 4.09%. Remarkably, even with Group R fully shut off, the averaged ethylene yield increases by 3.86%, demonstrating that highly imbalanced heating strategy outperforms the conventional symmetric arrangement. Given the limited yield improvements achieved under the conventional framework over decades, a new operational philosophy for high-efficiency cracking furnaces is warranted.

item.title: Inverse theoretical spectroscopy via Monte Carlo sampling: From spectra to ensembles of molecular conformations
item.description: A molecule’s structure determines its spectroscopic properties, and vice versa, molecular spectra are indispensable for elucidating its three-dimensional structure. Here, we present a Monte Carlo sampling scheme for generating an ensemble of molecular structures that is compatible with an ensemble of spectra around a given reference spectrum. By analyzing this spectrally-constrained ensemble, we can determine which structural changes are compatible with the given reference spectrum. By constraining the spectrum only in selected windows, a more fine-grained analysis of selected spectral features becomes possible. We explore our spectral Monte Carlo sampling method for the dye molecule DFHBI, considering its electronic excitation spectrum. We find that the conformational space of molecular structures with similar spectra is vast, and we identify high-energy distorted structures whose spectra closely match that of the ground-state structure. Our method provides a novel, ensemble-based perspective on the inverse mapping from spectra to molecular structures.

item.title: The Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation in Quantum Chemistry: Symmetrized Riesz Exchange Kernels, Sobolev Domain Classification, and O(N4) Quasiparticle Electronic Structure across Bond Dissociation
item.description: A central challenge in ab initio electronic structure theory is capturing both short-range dynamic electron correlation (the Kato inter-electronic cusp) and long-range static multireference correlation across covalent bond dissociation without incurring the exponential O(exp N) cost of Full Configuration Interaction (FCI), the O(N⁶) cost and single-reference breakdown of Coupled Cluster Singles and Doubles (CCSD), or the one-electron self-interaction error (SIE) of Density Functional Theory (DFT). In this work (the first of two companion papers on the Multi-Electron Unified Wave Equation, MEUWE), we formulate and rigorously analyze the closed-system stationary sector of MEUWE as an ab initio two-electron correlation theory. First, we establish a foundational No-Go result against nonlinear state powers Ψᵖ (p ≠ 1) and unscaled nonlocal kernels (Proposition II.1), and establish operator uniqueness of the Jordan-symmetrized Riesz exchange kernel K̂sym = ½ ∑ᵢ₍ⱼ₎ {Ŵᵢ, r₀ᵅ|rᵢ − rⱼ|⁻ᵅ P̂ᵢⱼ} within the bilinear screening-permutation pencil P_W,K, showing that unsymmetrized operators ŴᵢV̂ᵅP̂ᵢⱼ violate Hermiticity (ΔHerm ∈ [1.68, 3.76]) and leak fermion states outside the Pauli sector ∧ᴺL²(R³) (Theorem III.1). Second, we establish a four-regime functional-analytic self-adjointness classification of Ĥ₀ + ΛK̂sym on ∧ᴺL²(R³): operator Kato–Rellich self-adjointness on H²(R³ᴺ) for α ∈ (0, 3/2), quadratic-form KLMN self-adjointness on H¹(R³ᴺ) via Hardy’s inequality for α ∈ [3/2, 2) (including our canonical α = 3/2), the critical Hardy threshold at α = 2, and bounded-density L¹ ∩ L∞ expectation finiteness for α ∈ (2, 3) with ultraviolet divergence at α ≥ 3. Third, for closed bound states below the excitation threshold (Eₙ < Eₜₕ), we prove via Feshbach–Schur resolvent projection that integrating out the virtual excitation continuum yields a strictly real, Hermitian, energy-dispersive quasiparticle self-energy Σₘₑₘ(E) = Λγₘₑₘ(E)K̂sym whose self-consistent fixed point converges geometrically via Banach contraction (qₘₐₓ = 0.091226 < 1, error 4.44 × 10⁻¹⁵ Ha in ≤ 13 iterations, matching exact Stinespring resolvent poles to 5.82 × 10⁻⁷ Ha, Theorem III.5). Fourth, using exact 6D Mellin–Laplace Gaussian integrals implemented in PySCF/libcint, we verify that MEUWE is 100% self-interaction-free on all one-electron ions Z = 1 … 6 (|ΔE| ≤ 2.66 × 10⁻¹² mHa) and achieves an overall correlation RMSE of 0.3824 mHa across the Z = 2 … 6 two-electron isoelectronic series (7.31× more accurate than MP2, Section III C 1). Finally, freezing all parameters strictly at the two-electron Helium calibration (α = 1.50, μ = 0.606503, Λ₀ = 0.01150) with zero molecule-fitted parameters and zero FCI calls, our standalone O(N⁴) Dyson pair solver reproduces exact FCI potential energy surfaces across H₂, HeH⁺, and LiH (R ∈ [0.5, 3.0] Å) with mean absolute errors of 0.1382, 0.1618, and 0.1302 mHa, captures the avoided-crossing ionic-to-neutral dipole turnover in LiH (μ(3.0 Å) = 5.0398 D vs. FCI 5.0265 D where RHF diverges to 9.1647 D, Section III C 2), and resolves atomic K/L shell structures and Coulson–Neilson Coulomb holes across H–Ne (Section III C 3).

item.title: ChemEidos: Synthesis-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models for Domain-Specific Generative Design
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence models for de novo drug discovery often suffer synthetic tractability issues and lack fidelity in underrepresented chemical domains. This white paper highlights ChemEidos, a novel multimodal generative design platform that utilizes the underlying patterns, forms, and organizing principles of chemical space (eidos) by incorporating expert domain knowledge in focused training sets and at inference time.

item.title: Transferable Quasiparticle Correlation, Subtractive Multireference Embedding for Biradicaloid Ozone, and Retarded Casimir–Polder Dispersion in Multi-Electron Systems
item.description: Listing 1Computing accurate electron correlation across closed-shell polyatomics, multireference biradicaloids, and non-covalent van der Waals complexes represents a fundamental challenge in quantum chemistry. In this work, we investigate a transferable range-separated quasiparticle framework for molecular electronic structure and dispersion. First, for closed-shell polyatomics (CH4, NH3, H2O, CO2), the range-separated quasiparticle Dyson denominator parameters (mu = 0.50, alpha_sr = 1.35 a_0^-1, lambda_mu = 0.38) established on two-electron calibration benchmarks are transferred without molecule-specific re-optimization to 10- to 24-electron molecules, achieving an out-of-sample correlation energy Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 5.809 mHa vs. CCSD(T) across 6-31G* and cc-pVDZ basis sets (a 2.69x improvement over MP2 and 2.04x over CCSD). Second, for the multireference biradicaloid ozone molecule (O3, 1 1A_1), subtractive CASCI embedding accurately captures static correlation across the 11-point bending potential energy curve (theta_OOO in [105 deg, 130 deg], MAE 1.137 mHa), predicting an equilibrium bond angle of 116.755 deg (experiment 116.78 deg) and resolving the Hartree-Fock permanent dipole anomaly (0.5526 D vs. experiment 0.5337 D, where RHF diverges to 0.7937 D). Finally, we evaluate long-range non-covalent dispersion by combining Time-Dependent Hartree-Fock (TDHF) dynamic polarizabilities with a fractional memory retardation kernel and rational Becke-Johnson damping. We demonstrate that the memory kernel strictly screens dynamic polarizability relative to unretarded TDHF, with effective retardation coupling increasing systematically with monomer polarizability (0.02 a.u. for He, 0.05 a.u. for H2, and 0.08 a.u. for C2H4), yielding counterpoise-corrected binding curves for He2, (H2)2, and parallel-displaced pi-stacked ethylene dimers with MAEs of 0.0155, 0.0421, and 0.1336 kcal/mol vs. CCSD(T).

item.title: Airborne Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) in 20 Homes Several Months After the 2023 Maui Wildfires
item.description: Exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) is associated with adverse health outcomes, including cancer. PAHs are emitted by wildfires and may persist in indoor environments following smoke events. To better understand post-wildfire PAH persistence inside residences, we sampled for 16 airborne PAHs at 20 homes in Lāhainā, Hawaiʻi, 5-7 months after the 2023 Maui wildfires, both before and after deploying an additional air purifier on top of existing indoor filtration and purification systems. Additionally, we surveyed building occupants about pollution-relevant behaviors. Concentrations of all indoor airborne PAHs fell below risk-based screening levels. Estimated cumulative cancer risks and hazard indices were all below 1 × 10-6 and 1, respectively. We found higher concentrations of low-molecular-weight PAHs than highmolecular-weight PAHs. The results of source attribution using indoor/outdoor ratios, principal component analysis, and diagnostic ratios are somewhat equivocal, but we could not clearly identify a biomass-combustion-related source of the indoor airborne PAHs. We found little association between self-reported occupant behaviors and PAH levels, and we found no significant effect of the air purifier on indoor PAH concentraties. These results suggest that there was not substantial fire-related airborne PAH contamination inside local residences several months after a major wildfire event.

item.title: mzView : visualizing mass spectrometry data in the browser
item.description: Routine inspection of raw mass spectrometry data is limited to installed desktop software which often needs high memory, security updates, compatible operating system, and hard-drive space. Existing web-based tools require uploading raw data files to a server. To address this, we introduce mzView, a zero-installation web application featuring client-side modules for visualizing mass spectrometry data files covering Data Dependent Acquisition (DDA), Data Independent Acquisition (DIA), Imaging, and Ion-mobility acquisitions. mzView supports mzML, imzML, MSP, Bruker (.d) file formats. It enables multi-target extraction ion chromatograms (EICs) with MS2-event overlays and isotope- and adduct-driven EIC visualization ; global filtering of DDA MS2 spectra by precursor and fragment ions; DIA fragment EICs by isolation window and fragment co-occurrence; and rapid in-browser MSP library parsing and filtering. Ion-mobility and imaging data are visualized using WebGL GPU based faster rendering. To assist in spectra annotation, mzView searches spectra against the IDSL spectral database of over 50,000 compounds curated from publicly available mass spectral databases, scored by spectral entropy and cosine similarity with interactive mirror plots. Accepted hits can be saved to a browser-local annotation library, edited, re-searched, and exported as MSP files. Demonstrated on publicly available DDA and DIA data files of NIST SRM 1950 plasma acquired on a SCIEX ZenoTOF 8600, and additional data collected using Bruker timsTOF Metabo and MALDI- Pro Ultra 2 instruments, mzView readily handles files up to 35 GB, with indexing, filtering, and EIC extraction completing in less than 60 seconds. mzView is freely available at https://mzview.org (License: CC-BY).

item.title: Disentangling Between-Target and Within-Target Signal in PPI Benchmarking
item.description: Pooled correlation, the metric usually reported when predicting mutation effects on protein–protein binding affinity (ΔΔG), mixes two different capabilities: placing targets on a common binding scale and ranking mutations correctly within a target. We formulate an exact between-/within-target covariance decomposition for PPI ΔΔG benchmarking, r = C_B + C_W, and apply it to matched, provenance-filtered evaluation sets. In a controlled comparison that changes only the split regime, on identical 7,523 mutation rows and identical model configurations, median pooled Pearson falls from 0.6844 under random splitting to 0.1508 under family-out-of-distribution evaluation, with ΔC_B = −0.4347 and ΔC_W = −0.1011; the between-target component accounts for 81.1% of the summed absolute component change. Target weighting changes how the components should be read: across five schemes C_B reverses sign in 40/109 configurations and in 34/109 even above |C_B| > 0.005, whereas C_W reverses in only 5/109. Fixed-K shortlist metrics are constrained by candidate-set geometry: a rank-linear discriminability surrogate is zero when n ≤ K and peaks near n* ≈ 20.5 for K = 10, and 40.8% of targets with n ≥ 5 fall in that degenerate regime. A matched retrospective ablation separated modifications that improve pooled scores only from those that also improve within-target ranking. External evidence from five methods is underpowered and its apparent cross-axis agreement is not robust to score orientation. Benchmarks should therefore report both components under declared weighting and candidate-set geometry.

item.title: Aromaticity Hidden in Magnetically Antiaromatic Macrocycles
item.description: Global paratropic ring currents give norcorrole and rosarin a familiar antiaromatic label and account for their characteristic pattern of deshielded inner and shielded outer protons. Translating that magnetic picture into a perimeter of alternating double bonds, however, assigns the occupied 𝜋 electrons to a bonding pattern that the current pathway alone does not determine. Here we ask how much of the ground-state bonding the magnetic response actually reveals. For a diaza[16]annulene model series and for free-base and metal-coordinated porphyrinoids, we compare occupied bonding domains, resolved with the electron density of delocalized bonds and the bond delocalization function, with orbital-resolved magnetic response. A global paratropic pathway persists when the model bonding changes from a delocalized 16𝜋 perimeter to localized double bonds or two pyrrolic sextets. In norcorrole and rosarin, fixed sextets give way to migrating patterns upon coordination, again without changing the paratropic classification. Orbital decomposition reveals local diatropic contributions beneath the global response. Isomerizations involving the pyrrolic units of norcorrole cost more than the rim control, although their energies also contain structural and stereochemical effects. A paratropic ring current is therefore not, by itself, a bonding formula. Annulene-based aromaticity assignments should retain Hückel’s energetic logic, with electron counts and magnetic or spectroscopic fingerprints interpreted through the complete molecular electronic structure rather than substituted for appropriate energetic and, where relevant, thermodynamic characterization.
